content.text:
**I would request changes before treating this work as complete.** I reviewed all 21 PRs, #206–#226, against `origin/dev` at `7c6ec5122351`. The per-function separation is correct, and all 14 new DocsFn sites build. However, there are broken consumer examples, shared navigation defects, and substantial gaps in the requested documentation refresh.

1. **[P2] Existing sites still document APIs that no longer exist.**

   These are pre-existing inaccuracies left unresolved by work explicitly intended to bring those sites up to date.

   | PR | Verified remaining problem |
   |---|---|
   | **#207 AuthFn** | The [Next.js quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/8e142c2c8d7a8dbc762b07a2e4f760b0d118eef1/authfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/nextjs.md#L64-L74) imports nonexistent `toNext`. Current exports provide `toNextHandlers`. SvelteKit guides similarly use nonexistent `toSvelteKit`; another guide imports nonexistent `toNextSession`. |
   | **#214 FileFn** | [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/0dd2cbcb3361a607b0a9493318e12ea0ac99a276/filefn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L31-L38) imports `createLocalStorageAdapter` from `@superfunctions/storage`; it belongs to `@superfunctions/storage-local`. This repeats across framework quickstarts. Database guides also reference nonexistent `applySchemaToAdapter`, and processor examples use obsolete options. |
   | **#211 DataFn** | The [plugin example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4f34c1bc46afc0c1830385c119594fac8f088427/datafn/docs/content/docs/reference/events.mdx#L60-L85) supplies a `hooks` array. Current `DatafnPlugin` requires `runsOn` and named callbacks such as `beforeMutation`; it has no `hooks` property. |
   | **#223 SearchFn** | The [Hono quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/hono.mdx#L27-L47) calls `sf.adapter.initialize`, but the server exposes only `router` and `close`. It also passes a plain object where the router expects a Web `Request`. Similar patterns remain in other TypeScript quickstarts. |

   Adding administration pages or refreshing Python guides does not complete the existing-site refresh while these primary consumer paths remain broken.

2. **[P2] The shared new-site template has broken mobile navigation and missing search.**

   At a 390px viewport, tapping **Menu** opens the backdrop and sets `aria-expanded=true`, but the drawer remains `display:none` with zero dimensions. The imported DocsFn theme hides the sidebar below 1024px, and the open state never restores its display.

   Desktop testing also found no search trigger or dialog; keyboard shortcuts did nothing after hydration. The integration is in [the shared layout](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/7f6d58a01cc9292a9df822e2019062644417c15a/apifn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte#L17-L31).

   I reproduced these on ApiFn. All 14 new sites copy the same relevant template, styles, and dependency pins, so the correction needs to cover that entire group.

3. **[P2] McpFn’s quickstart is not import-safe or usable by its manifest tooling — #218.**

   The [example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/fb63627965d95af2772465292dc835b8a86cfea7/mcpfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L45-L55) exports a named `declaration` and starts stdio at module scope, immediately before claiming the declaration is safe to import.

   The CLI loader consumes the default export or module itself. Running the documented example through `mcpfn manifest` reproduced **`Unsupported McpFn manifest formatVersion`**. Default-export the declaration from an import-safe module and put `serveStdio()` in a separate entrypoint.

4. **[P2] MemoryFn’s MCP example closes the server immediately after starting it — #220.**

   The [example’s `finally` block](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/5adfb40aa5ba628e392d0b21f4fe3802bb21867b/memoryfn/docs/content/docs/mcp.md#L18-L23) closes both the adapter and memory after `await adapter.start()`.

   `start()` resolves when the transport connects; it does not wait for the server’s lifetime. Consequently, this example immediately shuts down the service it just exposed. Cleanup should run when the host shuts down.

5. **[P2] SendFn’s Express mounting example imports a nonexistent function — #225.**

   The [reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b6bcdf8253b37a35d7889f20285a343b5b0ec23a/sendfn/docs/content/docs/reference/typescript.md#L100-L104) imports `createExpressApp` from `@superfunctions/http-express`. That package exports `toExpress`, not an application factory.

   Consumers need to construct an Express application and mount `toExpress(client.router)`. The supplied example cannot compile.

6. **[P2] DevFn’s getting-started sequence never writes the configuration it subsequently loads — #212.**

   The [command sequence](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b84bae1bb33e27220c1eab26184717ea1b50deba/devfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L8-L16) runs `init`, then `doctor --trust`.

   Without `--yes`, `init` only returns a preview with `written:false`. A fresh consumer therefore reaches `doctor` without a manifest. Include the explicit review-and-accept step, `init --yes`, before continuing.

7. **[P2] SearchFn’s FastAPI example exposes its captured handler as a request parameter — #223.**

   In the [route registration example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/fastapi.mdx#L20-L31), `_handler=handler` appears in the endpoint signature. FastAPI interprets it as a query parameter.

   I reproduced a successful normal request becoming **HTTP 500** with `?_handler=test`, because the code then calls a string. OpenAPI also exposes `_handler`. Capture the handler through a factory closure, outside the endpoint signature.

8. **[P2] CliFn’s Commander example fails typechecking and does not propagate the action’s exit status — #210.**

   The [callback](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/c5b7f17db7cd64c3e032b291c7a1abaf6eccac74/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md#L124-L136) returns `runAction()`, producing `Promise<number>`. Commander requires `void | Promise<void>`; a focused compilation with Commander 12 reproduced TS2345.

   Await the result, assign the returned status to `process.exitCode`, and show the asynchronous parsing entrypoint.

9. **[P2] Several new sites are outlines rather than comprehensive consumer documentation.**

   Concrete examples:

   - **#219 MDFN:** 38 pages contain only one code example. The [React reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4affc4c9dbb4d5eb2385e3999d15b04bf662f851/mdfn/docs/content/docs/reference/react.md#L6-L10) is a short description without imports, component usage, or props. The framework guide redirects readers to repository examples instead of teaching installation and mounting.
   - **#216 LangFn:** [Models and providers](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/9d1d3332748ca3692eeabfb339a75c53c9ede976/langfn/docs/content/docs/models-and-providers.md#L8-L12) lists capabilities and links source exports, but never demonstrates constructing a real provider.
   - **#221 PlugFn:** [Connections and OAuth](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b975ed8b01eeadebf6412f2ce9a5988dd31884d9/plugfn/docs/content/docs/connections-and-oauth.md#L8-L12) and workflow documentation describe capabilities without executable connection, action, or workflow examples.

   These need complete consumer journeys with setup, invocation, expected results, and failure handling.

10. **[P3] ReviewFn documents the wrong evidence directory — #222.**

    [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/f944b66d411b9bb0c067830bb258e0b4e45ffe4a/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L17) says evidence is stored under `.reviewfn/artifacts`. The CLI writes retained evidence under the output directory, defaulting to **`.reviewfn/output/artifacts`**.

The per-function separation is correct, and all 14 new DocsFn sites build. However, there are broken consumer examples, shared navigation defects, and substantial gaps in the requested documentation refresh.

1. **[P2] Existing sites still document APIs that no longer exist.**

   These are pre-existing inaccuracies left unresolved by work explicitly intended to bring those sites up to date.

   | PR | Verified remaining problem |
   |---|---|
   | **#207 AuthFn** | The [Next.js quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/8e142c2c8d7a8dbc762b07a2e4f760b0d118eef1/authfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/nextjs.md#L64-L74) imports nonexistent `toNext`. Current exports provide `toNextHandlers`. SvelteKit guides similarly use nonexistent `toSvelteKit`; another guide imports nonexistent `toNextSession`. |
   | **#214 FileFn** | [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/0dd2cbcb3361a607b0a9493318e12ea0ac99a276/filefn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L31-L38) imports `createLocalStorageAdapter` from `@superfunctions/storage`; it belongs to `@superfunctions/storage-local`. This repeats across framework quickstarts. Database guides also reference nonexistent `applySchemaToAdapter`, and processor examples use obsolete options. |
   | **#211 DataFn** | The [plugin example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4f34c1bc46afc0c1830385c119594fac8f088427/datafn/docs/content/docs/reference/events.mdx#L60-L85) supplies a `hooks` array. Current `DatafnPlugin` requires `runsOn` and named callbacks such as `beforeMutation`; it has no `hooks` property. |
   | **#223 SearchFn** | The [Hono quickstart](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/hono.mdx#L27-L47) calls `sf.adapter.initialize`, but the server exposes only `router` and `close`. It also passes a plain object where the router expects a Web `Request`. Similar patterns remain in other TypeScript quickstarts. |

   Adding administration pages or refreshing Python guides does not complete the existing-site refresh while these primary consumer paths remain broken.

2. **[P2] The shared new-site template has broken mobile navigation and missing search.**

   At a 390px viewport, tapping **Menu** opens the backdrop and sets `aria-expanded=true`, but the drawer remains `display:none` with zero dimensions. The imported DocsFn theme hides the sidebar below 1024px, and the open state never restores its display.

   Desktop testing also found no search trigger or dialog; keyboard shortcuts did nothing after hydration. The integration is in [the shared layout](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/7f6d58a01cc9292a9df822e2019062644417c15a/apifn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte#L17-L31).

   I reproduced these on ApiFn. All 14 new sites copy the same relevant template, styles, and dependency pins, so the correction needs to cover that entire group.

3. **[P2] McpFn’s quickstart is not import-safe or usable by its manifest tooling — #218.**

   The [example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/fb63627965d95af2772465292dc835b8a86cfea7/mcpfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L45-L55) exports a named `declaration` and starts stdio at module scope, immediately before claiming the declaration is safe to import.

   The CLI loader consumes the default export or module itself. Running the documented example through `mcpfn manifest` reproduced **`Unsupported McpFn manifest formatVersion`**. Default-export the declaration from an import-safe module and put `serveStdio()` in a separate entrypoint.

4. **[P2] MemoryFn’s MCP example closes the server immediately after starting it — #220.**

   The [example’s `finally` block](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/5adfb40aa5ba628e392d0b21f4fe3802bb21867b/memoryfn/docs/content/docs/mcp.md#L18-L23) closes both the adapter and memory after `await adapter.start()`.

   `start()` resolves when the transport connects; it does not wait for the server’s lifetime. Consequently, this example immediately shuts down the service it just exposed. Cleanup should run when the host shuts down.

5. **[P2] SendFn’s Express mounting example imports a nonexistent function — #225.**

   The [reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b6bcdf8253b37a35d7889f20285a343b5b0ec23a/sendfn/docs/content/docs/reference/typescript.md#L100-L104) imports `createExpressApp` from `@superfunctions/http-express`. That package exports `toExpress`, not an application factory.

   Consumers need to construct an Express application and mount `toExpress(client.router)`. The supplied example cannot compile.

6. **[P2] DevFn’s getting-started sequence never writes the configuration it subsequently loads — #212.**

   The [command sequence](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b84bae1bb33e27220c1eab26184717ea1b50deba/devfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L8-L16) runs `init`, then `doctor --trust`.

   Without `--yes`, `init` only returns a preview with `written:false`. A fresh consumer therefore reaches `doctor` without a manifest. Include the explicit review-and-accept step, `init --yes`, before continuing.

7. **[P2] SearchFn’s FastAPI example exposes its captured handler as a request parameter — #223.**

   In the [route registration example](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/ff280cff49c21de47a2c2fa5a023723b008294e3/searchfn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/fastapi.mdx#L20-L31), `_handler=handler` appears in the endpoint signature. FastAPI interprets it as a query parameter.

   I reproduced a successful normal request becoming **HTTP 500** with `?_handler=test`, because the code then calls a string. OpenAPI also exposes `_handler`. Capture the handler through a factory closure, outside the endpoint signature.

8. **[P2] CliFn’s Commander example fails typechecking and does not propagate the action’s exit status — #210.**

   The [callback](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/c5b7f17db7cd64c3e032b291c7a1abaf6eccac74/clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md#L124-L136) returns `runAction()`, producing `Promise<number>`. Commander requires `void | Promise<void>`; a focused compilation with Commander 12 reproduced TS2345.

   Await the result, assign the returned status to `process.exitCode`, and show the asynchronous parsing entrypoint.

9. **[P2] Several new sites are outlines rather than comprehensive consumer documentation.**

   Concrete examples:

   - **#219 MDFN:** 38 pages contain only one code example. The [React reference](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/4affc4c9dbb4d5eb2385e3999d15b04bf662f851/mdfn/docs/content/docs/reference/react.md#L6-L10) is a short description without imports, component usage, or props. The framework guide redirects readers to repository examples instead of teaching installation and mounting.
   - **#216 LangFn:** [Models and providers](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/9d1d3332748ca3692eeabfb339a75c53c9ede976/langfn/docs/content/docs/models-and-providers.md#L8-L12) lists capabilities and links source exports, but never demonstrates constructing a real provider.
   - **#221 PlugFn:** [Connections and OAuth](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/b975ed8b01eeadebf6412f2ce9a5988dd31884d9/plugfn/docs/content/docs/connections-and-oauth.md#L8-L12) and workflow documentation describe capabilities without executable connection, action, or workflow examples.

   These need complete consumer journeys with setup, invocation, expected results, and failure handling.

10. **[P3] ReviewFn documents the wrong evidence directory — #222.**

    [Getting started](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/f944b66d411b9bb0c067830bb258e0b4e45ffe4a/reviewfn/docs/content/docs/getting-started.md#L17) says evidence is stored under `.reviewfn/artifacts`. title: DB adapters
description: Configure the shared database adapter and provision FileFn tables.
---

# DB adapters

FileFn accepts `Adapter` from `@superfunctions/db`. Use `memoryAdapter` for disposable local state or `drizzleAdapter` for PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite.

```ts
import { memoryAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory";
const db = memoryAdapter();
```

The published entrypoints are `@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory` and `@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle`. There are no separate `@superfunctions/db-postgres`, `db-sqlite`, or `db-drizzle` packages in this source tree.

## Schema and migrations

```ts
import { getSchema } from "@filefn/server";
const { version, schemas } = getSchema({ namespace: "filefn" });
console.log(version, schemas.map((table) => table.modelName));
```

This returns seven table descriptors, including fields and indexes. It does not provision a database. Translate/review these descriptors in your host's migration tooling and apply the migration before serving FileFn requests. The Drizzle adapter reports `schema.migrations: false`; it does not implement automatic DDL. Keep the namespace used in your migrations and `createFileFn` identical.

FileFn wraps the supplied adapter with its schema internally. For a custom adapter, implement the exported `Adapter` type rather than a positional CRUD interface: methods receive objects such as `findOne({ model, where })` and `create({ model, data })`. Respect the adapter's transaction and constraint capabilities; pretending to support transactions can break consistency guarantees.

See [Drizzle](./db-drizzle), [PostgreSQL](./db-postgres), [SQLite](./db-sqlite), and the [schema reference](../reference/schema).
''')

title: Drizzle DB adapter
description: Use the shared Drizzle adapter with PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite.

# Drizzle DB adapter

```sh
npm install @superfunctions/db drizzle-orm pg
```

```ts
import { Pool } from "pg";
import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "@superfunctions/db/adapters/drizzle";

const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });

// Pass db to createFileFn({ db, storage, ... }).
```

Use dialect `postgres`, `mysql`, or `sqlite` with the corresponding Drizzle driver. The host owns the connection lifecycle; close the pool during application shutdown.

Use `getSchema({ namespace })` from `@filefn/server` as the source of table/field/index descriptors. Generate and review your host migrations, then apply them before running FileFn. Constructing the adapter or FileFn does not create SQL tables. The adapter does not expose an `applySchemaToAdapter` helper or automatic migration support.

See [DB adapters](./db) for the schema contract and [SQLite](./db-sqlite) for a local SQL configuration.
''')

title: CDN integration
description: Separate storage authorization from public asset delivery.
---

# CDN integration

The S3 and R2 adapters expose storage operations and signed URLs. They do not accept `cdnPrefix` or rewrite signed storage URLs to a CDN domain. Provision and configure your CDN in the host infrastructure, and choose an authorization model appropriate to public or private assets.

For private files, call FileFn's authorized download-resolution APIs. Preserve the returned URL, request headers, and expiry. Replacing the hostname of a signed URL can invalidate the signature or bypass the intended access policy. Use a host-owned adapter or delivery service if the CDN needs a different signing protocol.

## Route policies to configured storage targets

```ts
import { createRoutedStorageAdapter } from "@superfunctions/storage";
import { createS3StorageAdapter } from "@superfunctions/storage-s3";
import { createLocalStorageAdapter } from "@superfunctions/storage-local";

const storage = createRoutedStorageAdapter({
  defaultTarget: "durable",
  adapters: {
    durable: createS3StorageAdapter({ bucket: process.env.S3_BUCKET!, region: process.env.AWS_REGION! }),
    temporary: createLocalStorageAdapter({ rootDir: "./.filefn-storage" }),
  },
});
```

Policies select a registered target through `storageTarget` and `artifactStorageTarget`. The router uses an explicit adapter map and `defaultTarget`; it has no arbitrary per-request `resolveTarget` callback. Validate environment variables before constructing adapters.

Public CDN delivery is a separate host policy: publish only objects intended to be public, configure cache keys and content headers, and plan invalidation when replacing or removing content. Do not expose private storage keys or long-lived credentials to the browser. See [downloads](/docs/features/downloads) and [storage targets](/docs/core-concepts/storage-targets).
''')

The router has no `resolveTarget` callback. Keep tenant authorization in the host and do not accept an arbitrary adapter/target from the client. See [CDN and storage routing](/docs/recipes/cdn-integration).

'''+s[b:];p.write_text(s)

The search artifact is already fetched separately via the /search.json endpoint (DocsSiteSearch.svelte), and the docs page loader only uses counts of it (searchDocumentCount/searchScopes), so every page load ships the whole search index plus manifest as redundant payload that grows linearly with the number of docs pages. Return a slim projection from the layout (siteTitle, canonicalUrl, compatPreset, config/navigation) and keep manifest/searchArtifact server-only; the layout only consumes data.source.config and data.source.siteTitle today.

    source: {
      siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      compatPreset: source.compatPreset,
      config: source.config,
    },
  };
};

The search artifact is already fetched separately via the /search.json endpoint (DocsSiteSearch.svelte), and the docs page loader only uses counts of it (searchDocumentCount/searchScopes), so every page load ships the whole search index plus manifest as redundant payload that grows linearly with the number of docs pages. Return a slim projection from the layout (siteTitle, canonicalUrl, compatPreset, config/navigation) and keep manifest/searchArtifact server-only; the layout only consumes data.source.config and data.source.siteTitle today.

      compatPreset: source.compatPreset,
      config: source.config,
    },
  };
};

      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      compatPreset: source.compatPreset,

P3: Every page in this concatenated file renders its title twice: the generated header block (`# <title>` + the frontmatter `description` blockquote) is immediately followed by the body's own `# <title>` H1, which the source pages still carry in frontmatter plus body. For an LLM single-shot context this adds ~19 redundant title/description pairs and a confusing doubled heading on each page. Drop the body H1 from the source content files (or strip it in the generation pipeline) so each page appears once.


34 False apifn/docs/src/routes/+layout.server.ts 7 


P3: Returning the whole `source` (full docs manifest, complete `searchArtifact`, config) from the root `+layout.server.ts` serializes all of it into the client data payload on every page load, while the client components only read `data.source.config` and `data.source.siteTitle` (`+layout.svelte` lines 29/35, `+page.svelte` lines 11/30/31). The search artifact is already fetched separately by `DocsSiteSearch` via `/search.json`. As the corpus grows this bloat grows with it; keep the layout return to the small config subset the client needs and let server-only consumers (`docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts`) call the memoized `loadDocsSiteSource()` directly instead of via `parent()`.


35 False apifn/docs/package.json 31 


P3: `test` runs `vitest run` but `vitest` is not declared in this package's dependencies/devDependencies; the command only resolves because `vitest` is hoisted from the root workspace's devDependencies. A standalone install or later un-hoist breaks the script. Add `vitest` to devDependencies.


36 False apifn/docs/src/routes/+page.svelte 12 


P3: `$derived` values are read-only, so declare them with `const`, not `let`. This matches Svelte 5 guidance and the convention used everywhere else in this repo; `let` allows accidental reassignment that the compiler can't flag.


37 False apifn/docs/src/routes/+page.server.ts 5 


P3: This `load` is a no-op: SvelteKit already merges a layout server load's data into the page's `data` prop and into the generated `PageData` type, so `data.source` is typed and available on the home route without any page-level load. The comment's rationale for the function is incorrect. Drop the function and this file, or only keep it with a corrected comment if a page-specific load is planned later.

Every target in this package table is a directory, but GitHub's `/blob/dev/...` route is for files, so these links lead readers to a not-found page. Use `/tree/dev/apifn/...` for directory links; the same broken transformation also appears for the Python SDK, the Svelte package link, and the mock/snippets links in `reference/cli.md` (while the workflow file link should remain `/blob/`).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

P1: Removing the hydration guard causes DocsSiteSearch to render during SSR, yet the two other docs sites consuming the same shared Search component (scripts/docs-site/Search.svelte) — authfn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte and filefn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte — still defer it behind onMount. The removed comment explicitly cites SSR incompatibility as the reason for the deferral, and a SvelteKit `vite build` does not necessarily execute SSR for non-prerendered routes, so the passing build does not prove the SSR path is safe. # Python SDK

The `apifn/python` package provides Python helpers for OpenAPI generation, diffing, collections, FastAPI, and Flask. It requires Python 3.10 or newer and has its own version lifecycle, separate from the npm packages.

See the [Python source package](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/apifn/python) for its current public exports, installation metadata, and examples. The TypeScript CLI and Python helpers can consume the same OpenAPI contract, but do not assume their release versions match.

# @apifn/react

React UI components for ApiFn. Render an interactive API explorer — endpoint docs, a live Try-It console, schema viewer, request history, response diffing, and performance overlays — from any OpenAPI document.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @apifn/react
```

`react` and `react-dom` (`^18` or `^19`) are peer dependencies.

## Components

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `ApiExplorer` | Full explorer shell (sidebar + tabs) — the all-in-one entry point |
| `EndpointViewer` | Documentation for a single operation (params, body, responses) |
| `SchemaViewer` | Collapsible JSON-schema tree |
| `TryIt` | Live request console with auth, params, and body |
| `RequestHistory` | List of past requests with expandable detail |
| `ResponseDiff` | Side-by-side diff of two responses |
| `PerformanceOverlay` | Latency/throughput KPIs and bar charts |

---

## Quick Start

```tsx
import { ApiExplorer } from "@apifn/react";

export function Docs({ spec }) {
  return <ApiExplorer spec={spec} baseUrl="https://api.example.com" theme="dark" showHistory />;
}
```

### ApiExplorer props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

 0  billfn/docs/content/docs/server/administration.mdx 26 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clarify that catalog reads are instance-wide**

For hosts that share one `BillFnInstance` across multiple administration scopes, this overstates the subject isolation: `listProducts`/`getProduct`, `listPlans`/`getPlan`, and `listPrices`/`getPrice` call `billfn.getCatalog()` without invoking the configured `subject` resolver (`billfn/admin/src/domain-service.ts:158-184`). Only subscriptions, entitlements, and usage are actually resolved against the active subject, so document the first three resources as instance-wide catalog data rather than implying that the subject binding scopes them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

 1  billfn/docs/content/docs/server/administration.mdx 26 


P2: Products, plans, and prices come from the configured catalog, not the active subject. Distinguish those reads from subject-scoped subscriptions, entitlements, and usage so users do not assume the catalog varies by scope.



 2  billfn/docs/content/docs/server/administration.mdx 22 Scope authorization cannot rely on `resolveAuthorizedBillableSubject` alone: the product, plan, and price handlers never call that resolver, and the shared dispatcher's default policy checks permission, not whether the actor owns the selected scope. An integration that authorizes only inside this callback would allow catalog operations under an unauthorized scope; please explicitly require a dispatcher policy or equivalent host check for **every** operation, and describe catalog reads as global rather than subject-scoped.

P2: The bundled provider populates `absolutePath` with a collection-relative label instead of the actual configured source path. Preserve the real `content/docs/...` or `static/...` path (and pass it through the other entry constructors) so downstream metadata and edit links identify the source file correctly.



 1  botfn/docs/tsconfig.json 26 


P2: This `include` block replaces (not augments) the `include` from the extended `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` — TypeScript does not merge `include`/`exclude` across `extends`, exactly the pitfall the SvelteKit scaffold comment warns about. It drops `.svelte-kit/ambient.d.ts`, `.svelte-kit/non-ambient.d.ts`, and `.svelte-kit/types/**` from the program, so the generated `$env/*` ambient modules and other `.svelte-kit` declarations no longer resolve or get type-checked; the first route that imports `$env/...` will silently fail in the editor and in `svelte-check`. Every other SvelteKit app in this repo (superconsole/tsconfig.json, filefn/examples/full-demo/client/tsconfig.json) extends `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` without overriding `include`. Add the generated globs here, or drop the `include` block entirely so the generated config's includes apply.



 2  botfn/docs/content/docs/reference/commands-and-routes.md 11 


P3: The four Discord slash commands are listed in the same "Entry" column as real HTTP routes (`POST /interactions`, `POST /slack/events`, `/trpc/*`), and the `/-prefixed` form makes them easy to mistake for endpoints. The note at the end disambiguates only the admin capabilities. Add a similar note clarifying that the `/link-*` and `/create-*` entries are registered command names handled inside `POST /interactions`, not separate routes.



 3  botfn/docs/README.md 12 


P3: `docsfn` won't resolve in a fresh shell: the binary only exists in `botfn/docs/node_modules/.bin` (from the `@docsfn/cli` devDependency), which isn't on `PATH` after `npm install`, so `docsfn validate --root .` fails with "command not found" unless invoked through npm/npx. Docs sites in this repo (authfn/docs, filefn/docs) don't document a bare `docsfn` invocation either. Run it as `npx docsfn validate --root .`, or add a `validate` npm script (e.g. `docsfn validate --root .`) and document `npm run validate`.



 4  botfn/docs/content/docs/integrations.md 8 


P3: The returned `body` is a parsed, Zod-validated object (`DiscordInteractionBody`), not the raw request body — the raw text was consumed by `request.text()`, and Zod's default behavior strips keys not in the schema. Saying "fresh request body" implies raw-body equivalence; a downstream handler that re-serializes or inspects fields outside the schema will not get the original body. Recommend phrasing like "pass the parsed interaction body to downstream handlers" to avoid implying raw-body fidelity.



 5  botfn/docs/content/docs/persistence.md 15 


P3: The example references an undeclared `persistenceServiceUrl`, so the snippet will not compile as written. Use the established environment binding `env.PERSISTENCE_SERVICE_URL` (as in SETUP.md and the `discord-bot.md` setup section) instead of an undefined placeholder.



 6  botfn/docs/docsfn.config.ts 8 


P3: `site.canonicalUrl` is not set, so `generate-llms.mjs` passes `canonicalUrl: undefined` into `buildLlmsTxtArtifacts`, and the committed `static/llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` are emitted with relative links (`/docs/admin`, `/docs/persistence`, ...). An LLM loading these files has no way to resolve those URLs. Both sibling sites that set `canonicalUrl` (authfn, filefn) emit absolute URLs in their `llms.txt`. The docs README notes this is deferred until the public host is assigned, but the key should be added before merge so the generated artifacts are usable and stay that way on every `prebuild` regeneration.



 7  botfn/docs/package.json 23 


P3: `@uifn/core` is never imported anywhere in botfn/docs — the site source only imports `@docsfn/*`, `@21n/fonts`, and SvelteKit packages. It is already installed transitively (`@docsfn/svelte` → `@uifn/svelte` → `@uifn/core`, per package-lock.json), so this direct devDependency is dead weight. Drop it unless something here is expected to use it.



 8  botfn/docs/package.json 10 


P3: The `test` script runs `vitest`, but `vitest` is not declared in this package's devDependencies — it only resolves via the root workspace's hoisted `vitest ^3.2.4`. A workspace-local install or removal of the root vitest would break `npm --workspace @botfn/docs test` with "vitest: command not found". Declare vitest in devDependencies.



 9 OUTDATED botfn/docs/src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts None 


P3: `getCompiledDocsPost`, `getDocsSiteCompiledCacheSummary`, `createDocsSearchRuntime`, and `DocsSiteCompiledCacheSummary` are exported but never consumed anywhere in `botfn/docs`, and the per-post compiled cache they read is never used by any route. Remove the unused exports and the posts-map cache, or wire them to a route.



 10  botfn/docs/tsconfig.json 21 


P3: With `"types": ["svelte", "vite/client"]` the automatic inclusion of `@types/*` global declarations is restricted, so the Node global `process` is undeclared. `svelte.config.js` is checked (`checkJs` + `allowJs`) and uses `process.env.CLOUDFLARE_DOCS_DEPLOY` twice, so editors and `svelte-check` will report `Cannot find name 'process'`. Add `"node"` to the `types` list (with `@types/node` as a devDependency) or drop the `types` field so Node globals are auto-included.



 11  botfn/docs/src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts 115 


P3: `searchDocumentCount`, `searchScopes`, and `compatPreset` are returned from the load function but the docs `+page.svelte` never reads them, so they are dead data serialized into every SSR payload. Drop them or consume them.



 12  botfn/docs/src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts 28 


P3: `isRouteNotFoundError` claims to narrow to `{ message: string }` but only checks the error `code`, so a `DOCS_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` error without a string `message` would be passed to `error(404, ...)` as a non-string. Verify `typeof message === "string"` in the guard.

🛑 Blocker — must fix before merge

**Known vulnerabilities in svelte@5.0.0**

OSV.dev reports 6 known vulnerabilities affecting `svelte@5.0.0`, introduced by this PR:

- [GHSA-crpf-4hrx-3jrp](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27125) **moderate**: Svelte SSR attribute spreading includes inherited properties from prototype chain — fixed in 5.51.5
- [GHSA-f7gr-6p89-r883](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27121) **moderate**: Svelte affected by cross-site scripting via spread attributes in Svelte SSR — fixed in 5.51.5
- [GHSA-m56q-vw4c-c2cp](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27122) **moderate**: Svelte SSR does not validate dynamic element tag names in `<svelte:element>` — fixed in 5.51.5

…and 3 more — see the OSV links above.

Upgrade to 5.51.5 or later.

 15  botfn/docs/content/docs/persistence.md 10 The instruction says to run `run deploy` from the repository root, but that isn't an executable shell command. Please spell out `npm --workspace @botfn/persistence-service run deploy` so the deployment step works when copied.

 16  botfn/docs/vite.config.ts 23 


P2: `import.meta.resolve("@docsfn/core/search-runtime")` and the core alias run at config-load time, so if @docsfn/core 0.0.5 doesn't export `./search-runtime` (or resolves to a package entry that changes), Node throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED here and both `vite dev` and `vite build` die at startup. Two things make this fragile: (1) no site source imports the subpath — `rg` shows the only reference to `search-runtime` in botfn/docs is this config line, while authfn/docs and filefn/docs build against @docsfn/core with just `ssr.noExternal(["@docsfn/core","@docsfn/svelte"])` and no aliases; (2) `import.meta.resolve` uses Node's default export conditions, so this single dist entry is then forced onto both the client and SSR bundles, bypassing Vite's conditional-exports resolution entirely. Drop these two aliases (and the comment) to match the working sibling-site setup, or if the pin is really required use the sibling pattern `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve(...)` and confirm the subpath is exported by the pinned version.



 17  botfn/docs/src/lib/components/DocsSiteSearch.svelte 2 


P3: `Search.svelte` is imported via a five-level relative path that escapes the SvelteKit project root (`botfn/docs`) into the workspace `scripts/` tree. Vite resolves it today because the workspace root is the fs-allow root, but the import bypasses the project structure and breaks the moment `botfn/docs` moves within the workspace. Every other cross-directory reference in this repo already goes through a Vite alias (botfn/docs/vite.config.ts defines `@searchfn/*` aliases; authfn and filefn resolve their shared search component via a `@site/docs-search` alias). Add the same style of alias (e.g. `@site/docs-search` -> `../../scripts/docs-site/Search.svelte`) in botfn/docs/vite.config.ts and import from it.

The layout server load returns the entire DocsSiteSource object — including the full manifest whose page entries carry every doc's raw markdown `body` (docs-site-source.ts:376) — on every request. SvelteKit serializes all server load data into the client payload, so every page response ships the whole site's content even though client components only consume siteTitle, site.description, topNav, and showFooter, inflating each SSR response and hydration payload with tens of KB of unused content. Project only the fields the client needs (e.g. return { siteTitle, siteDescription, topNav, showFooter, canonicalUrl }) and keep the full manifest server-side, retrieving it via a dedicated $lib/server import inside the docs page load where it is actually used.

```typescript
export const load: LayoutServerLoad = async () => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();
  return {
    source: {
      siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      config: {
        site: { title: source.config.site.title, description: source.config.site.description, showFooter: source.config.site.showFooter },
        navigation: source.config.navigation,
      },
    },
  };
};
```

The layout server load returns the entire DocsSiteSource object — including the full manifest whose page entries carry every doc's raw markdown `body` (docs-site-source.ts:376) — on every request. SvelteKit serializes all server load data into the client payload, so every page response ships the whole site's content even though client components only consume siteTitle, site.description, topNav, and showFooter, inflating each SSR response and hydration payload with tens of KB of unused content. Project only the fields the client needs (e.g. return { siteTitle, siteDescription, topNav, showFooter, canonicalUrl }) and keep the full manifest server-side, retrieving it via a dedicated $lib/server import inside the docs page load where it is actually used.

```typescript
export const load: LayoutServerLoad = async () => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();
  return {
    source: {
      siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      config: {
        site: { title: source.config.site.title, description: source.config.site.description, showFooter: source.config.site.showFooter },
        navigation: source.config.navigation,
      },
    },
  };
};
```

The layout server load returns the entire DocsSiteSource object, whose manifest entries include every docs page's full markdown body and whose searchArtifact embeds the whole search index. SvelteKit serializes layout load data into every page's client payload, so the full text of all documentation pages plus a duplicate of the search index (already served at /search.json) is shipped in the SSR HTML of every route, growing linearly with docs content size. Return only the fields the layout actually consumes (siteTitle, config.navigation, config.site) and fetch manifest/search data in the route-level loads that need it.

```typescript
export const load: LayoutServerLoad = async () => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();
  return {
    source: {
      siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      compatPreset: source.compatPreset,
      config: source.config, // pick only fields the layout renders (navigation, site)
    },
  };
};
```

`[...slug]` is a required rest parameter in SvelteKit: it matches `/docs/<something>` but not the bare `/docs` URL (the zero-segment case). The top nav item `Docs -> /docs`, `llms.txt`, and the `index.md` docs index all point at `/docs`, which will currently fall through to SvelteKit's generic 404. Rename the route directory to `[[...slug]]` (optional rest) and pass `params.slug ?? ""` so the index page resolves for zero segments.

```

The sentence `an invalid JSON or non-object shape raises InvalidConfigError` starts lowercase in the middle of the paragraph — publicly rendered documentation. Fix the capitalization, then regenerate `static/llms.txt` / `static/llms-full.txt` (`npm run generate:llms`) so the committed artifacts reflect the fix.

```suggestion
`createProjectConfig(path?)` provides a JSON store with `read`, `write`, `get`, and `set`. Supply a product-specific path; its default filename is Conduct-specific. An invalid JSON or non-object shape raises `InvalidConfigError`. It is separate from the discovered module loader.
```

---

When this workspace is built with Node 18.17 or 18.18—which the root `package.json` explicitly supports via `>=18.17.0`—`import.meta.resolve` is still gated by `--experimental-import-meta-resolve`, which Vite does not supply. Evaluating this config therefore fails before the documentation build starts. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

 23  clifn/docs/src/routes/+layout.svelte 24 


P1: This unconditionally makes `TopBar` render `DocsSiteSearch` during SSR, reintroducing the dialog's browser-only path and risking SSR failure or hydration errors on every page. Restore the `onMount` client guard, or make the search component explicitly SSR-safe before passing it to `TopBar`.



 24  clifn/docs/content/docs/reference/core-readme.md 127 


P2: The commander example now propagates the exit code via `process.exitCode = await runAction(...)`, but the `node:util.parseArgs` example in the same document (immediately after the `cac` section) still calls `await runAction(...)` as a bare statement. `runAction` returns `1` on action failure, and discarding that return value means a consumer copying the parseArgs pattern exits 0 even when the action fails. Apply the same `process.exitCode = await runAction(...)` propagation there (and likewise for the `cac` example, whose returned promise is not used as an exit code) so the fix is consistent across all three parser examples teaching consumers exit handling.



 25  clifn/docs/vite.config.ts 22 


P3: `import.meta.resolve` is unflagged only from Node 18.19.0 (and 20.6.0), but the root package.json declares `engines.node: ">=18.17.0"`. On Node 18.17–18.18 the config throws (`import.meta.resolve is not a function`) before Vite can build or run dev. Bump the engines floor to `>=18.19.0`, or resolve the package path with `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve(...)` instead.



 26  scripts/docs-site/runtime.ts 179 


P3: This new shared runtime duplicates the complete implementations still used by the AuthFn and FileFn sites, so fixes to manifest, search, or content loading can drift across three copies. Migrate the existing consumers to this runtime or keep the implementation in one shared module before merging.

---
title: Migration guide
description: Adopt DevFn without losing existing scripts, outputs, or Compose data.
---

1. Preserve all existing scripts and Compose data.
2. Run `devfn init`, inspect confirmed versus proposed detections, then rerun with `--yes` only when the preview is truthful.
3. Edit the manifest so every command, dependency, port, profile, and health check is explicit.
4. Run `devfn doctor --trust`; address missing runtimes and exact-port conflicts.
5. Before the first start, back up every pre-existing file targeted by `environmentOutputs[].path`; DevFn overwrites configured outputs and cannot restore prior contents.
6. Start with a minimal profile and compare it with the existing manual startup flow.
7. Add full, OAuth, test, or docs profiles incrementally. Public tunnels must remain explicit.
8. Verify `devfn down` preserves databases and volumes before adopting it as the daily command.

Rollback by running `devfn down`, then inspect `runtimeDir` and every `environmentOutputs[].path` in the manifest before removing generated files. The default generated location is `.devfn/`, but custom paths may live elsewhere. Preserve any target that existed before DevFn adoption; cleanup does not know whether a configured output replaced user-owned content. Finally remove the DevFn manifest and continue using the preserved original scripts. Docker volumes and source configuration are not deleted.
---
title: Configuration contract
description: Manifest fields, ports, processes, services, profiles, and policy.
---

DevFn discovers `devfn.config.ts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, or `.json` while walking upward from the current directory. JavaScript-family manifests are executable code, require digest-bound trust, and must be self-contained (no imports or `require()`). JSON is data-only.

## Top-level manifest

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version: 1` | yes | Manifest schema version. |
| `project.id` | yes | Stable semantic project identity. |
| `project.name` | no | Human display name. |
| `defaultProfile` | no | Profile selected when `--profile` is omitted. Without it, a `profiles.default` entry is required. |
| `runtimeDir` | no | Repository-relative generated-state root; defaults to `.devfn`. |
| `ports` | no | Named `PortSpec` map. |
| `processes` | no | Named native process map. |
| `services` | no | Named Docker Compose service map. |
| `profiles` | yes | Named selections of processes/services plus non-secret environment and proxy choice. |
| `hostnames` | no | Explicit local hostname routes to named ports. |
| `prerequisites` | no | Required command/version diagnostics, optionally profile-scoped. |
| `environmentOutputs` | no | Repository-relative dotenv or JSON runtime files and owner-only permission modes. |
| `policy` | no | Repository-relative organization policy JSON path. |

Every repository-relative path rejects absolute paths, `..` escape, and runtime symlink escape. References to ports, processes, services, profiles, dependencies, and hostname targets must resolve during validation. An explicitly configured but missing policy is an error; only the conventional unconfigured policy path is optional.

## Ports

A port can specify `protocol` (`tcp` or `udp`), `preferred`, `range: [start, end]`, `exact`, `ephemeral`, `exposure` (`loopback` or `public`), conventional container `internal` port, contiguous `block` name, and exported `env` key.

- `exact: true` requires `preferred` and fails closed on collision.
- `ephemeral: true` cannot be combined with fixed preferences.
- Requirements sharing `block` receive a contiguous allocation.
- Public ports require `devfn up --allow-public`.

## Native processes

`adapter` is one of `command`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `turbo`, `wrangler`, `xcode`, or `extfn`. A process can specify `command`, package-manager `script`, repository-relative `cwd`, non-secret literal `env`, inherited `envAllowlist`, redacted `secretEnv`, named `ports`, `dependsOn`, `health`, `shutdownTimeoutMs`, and `exposure` (`local` or `public`).

Turbo, Wrangler, and ExtFn resolve project-local binaries with offline npm execution; pnpm runs through Corepack so the repository's `packageManager` pin is honored. Adapters never download a missing tool during startup. `doctor` reports the missing prerequisite instead. Discovery marks Yarn and Bun as proposed and emits no guessed npm process; add an explicit command adapter after review.

Local-process exposure verification requires `lsof` on macOS and Linux; Windows uses `netstat`. Run `devfn doctor` before startup to detect a missing listener-inspection tool.

Sensitive-looking keys cannot be literal manifest values. They must be inherited by name in `envAllowlist` and repeated in `secretEnv`, which activates streaming redaction before logs are persisted. This is a key-name safeguard, not general secret detection; reviewers must inspect all other literal values. Public processes require `--allow-public`.

## Compose services

A service uses `adapter: "compose"`, Compose `service`, optional repository-relative `file`, project-name prefix, named host-port-to-container-port mappings, dependencies, health, `persistent`, non-secret `env`, `envAllowlist`, and `secretEnv`. DevFn always adds the worktree instance suffix to the Compose project name.

DevFn writes a generated override with loopback host mappings unless the named port explicitly selects public exposure. It starts only the requested service with `--no-deps`. Services declaring `secretEnv` use Docker's `none` logging driver and therefore cannot use log-pattern health checks. Ordinary cleanup stops/removes only invocation-owned containers and never passes a volume-deletion flag.

## Health checks

- HTTP: `{ type: "http", port: "app", path: "/health", expectedStatus: 200, timeoutMs: 120000 }`
- TCP: `{ type: "tcp", port: "postgres" }`
- Command: `{ type: "command", command: ["node", "scripts/ready.mjs"] }`
- Log: `{ type: "log", pattern: "ready on" }`

HTTP URLs are returned only for explicitly routed hostnames or ports named by HTTP health checks. Other services remain transport allocations visible through `devfn ports`; DevFn does not invent an HTTP URL for a database or arbitrary TCP listener.

## Profiles and hostnames

Profiles select named processes/services, add non-secret environment, and opt into the shared proxy with `proxy: true`. Dependencies are included transitively and started topologically. Cycles fail before mutation.

A hostname maps a route name to `target`, optional `hostname` template, `tls` (`off` or `internal`), and optional `profiles` filter. Templates accept `{project}` and `{instance}`. Every resolved name must end in `.localhost`.

## Organization policy

`devfn.policy.json` supports `fallbackRange`, `hostnameSuffix`, and entries with `name`, exactly one of `port`/`range`, `kind` (`protected`, `preferred`, or `excluded`), optional `project`, and `description`. `devfn ports report` combines the policy with the entire machine registry into Markdown; it is not limited to the current project or profile. `--output` must remain inside the repository.
---
title: Security contract
description: Manifest trust, secret handling, local exposure, and ownership.
---

- Every DevFn manifest can declare lifecycle commands, so the CLI refuses to load JSON, TypeScript, or JavaScript until the user records trust for its exact digest with `--trust`. JSON is parsed directly from the verified bytes; executable manifests run from a private copy of those same bytes and must be self-contained, with imports and `require()` rejected so dependency files cannot bypass the digest boundary.
- Runtime children inherit a small base environment plus explicit `envAllowlist` entries. Sensitive-looking keys must also be listed in `secretEnv`; a detached wrapper redacts those effective values before native-process logs are persisted. Literal values are rejected only when their key looks sensitive, so review every manifest literal. Compose logging is disabled for services with `secretEnv` because Docker otherwise retains historical unredacted logs. Secrets are not persisted in the registry or lifecycle receipt.
- Generated environment and state files use owner-only modes (default `0600`); their directories use `0700`. Existing files are explicitly re-permissioned after each write.
- Local ports and proxy targets bind to loopback unless a manifest explicitly selects public exposure. Profiles containing public processes or ports require the separate `--allow-public` confirmation on every start. A public Cloudflare tunnel must never be inferred.
- Repository-relative process, Compose, runtime, policy, and output paths are validated against lexical and symlink path escape.
- PID ownership uses a birth signature where the host exposes one. DevFn refuses to stop a reused PID.
- `down` stops only the exact worktree instance. Ordinary shutdown removes no persistent Docker volumes.
- Project hostnames must be concrete `.localhost` names. DevFn manages only a Caddy process it started itself and refuses to overwrite an unrelated Caddy admin endpoint.
- Volume deletion, database reset, public tunnels, and other destructive operations are outside ordinary lifecycle commands and require separate explicit tooling and confirmation.
---
title: Lifecycle and diagnostics
description: Start, inspect, stop, and recover one worktree instance.
---

`devfn up` plans resources in dependency order, reserves ports before mutation, starts selected native processes and Compose services, verifies readiness, registers proxy routes, and returns a machine-readable receipt. If an invocation fails, rollback targets resources created by that invocation. `status`, `logs`, and `doctor` expose live state and diagnostics; `down` stops only the exact worktree instance.

There is no background daemon in version 0.1. State, journals, logs, and generated environment files are kept under the configured runtime directory, `.devfn/` by default. Process ownership uses a PID birth signature where the host supplies one, so cleanup refuses a reused PID.

Ordinary `down` does not delete persistent Docker volumes. It is also not a general reset command. Explicit configured environment outputs may have overwritten files that existed before adoption; inspect them before manual cleanup. The [core package](/docs/reference/core), [process supervisor](/docs/reference/processes), and [migration guide](/docs/reference/migration) describe lifecycle boundaries.
# Shared DocsFn site runtime

The per-function sites supply their config and Vite raw-content globs to `createDocsSiteRuntime`. Each factory call owns its own manifest/search/compiled-content cache. Keep this module server-only; layout loaders return only site/navigation metadata, and search is loaded from `/search.json` when needed.

`Search.svelte` uses DocsFn's search runtime with a native modal dialog. It supports the visible trigger, Ctrl/Cmd+K, Escape, keyboard-focusable result links, loading state, and errors without the published UI dialog's SSR limitation.

Each site resolves the shared module's DocsFn imports through its own Vite aliases so it uses the versions pinned by that site. Run `npm run build` in the affected `<function>/docs` directory. After changing shared code, build all consumers and verify desktop search (including a result navigation and Escape) plus the mobile Menu drawer. Keep the responsive open-drawer override when using the current published theme.

The new-site PRs carry identical copies of this shared directory so they can land independently. Once merged, edits belong here rather than in the small per-site factory wrappers.

| `runtimeDir` | no | Repository-relative generated-state root; defaults to `.devfn`. |
| `ports` | no | Named `PortSpec` map. |
| `processes` | no | Named native process map. |
| `services` | no | Named Docker Compose service map. |
| `profiles` | yes | Named selections of processes/services plus non-secret environment and proxy choice. |
| `hostnames` | no | Explicit local hostname routes to named ports. |
| `prerequisites` | no | Required command/version diagnostics, optionally profile-scoped. |
| `environmentOutputs` | no | Repository-relative dotenv or JSON runtime files and owner-only permission modes. |
| `policy` | no | Repository-relative organization policy JSON path. |

Sensitive-looking keys cannot be literal manifest values. They must be inherited by name in `envAllowlist` and repeated in `secretEnv`, which activates streaming redaction before logs are persisted. - TCP: `{ type: "tcp", port: "postgres" }`

description: Manifest trust, secret handling, local exposure, and ownership.
---

HTTP URLs are returned only for explicitly routed hostnames or ports named by HTTP health checks. Other services remain transport allocations visible through `devfn ports`; DevFn does not invent an HTTP URL for a database or arbitrary TCP listener.

## Profiles and hostnames

Profiles select named processes/services, add non-secret environment, and opt into the shared proxy with `proxy: true`. Dependencies are included transitively and started topologically. Cycles fail before mutation.

A hostname maps a route name to `target`, optional `hostname` template, `tls` (`off` or `internal`), and optional `profiles` filter. Templates accept `{project}` and `{instance}`. Every resolved name must end in `.localhost`.

## Organization policy

`devfn.policy.json` supports `fallbackRange`, `hostnameSuffix`, and entries with `name`, exactly one of `port`/`range`, `kind` (`protected`, `preferred`, or `excluded`), optional `project`, and `description`. `devfn ports report` combines the policy with the entire machine registry into Markdown; it is not limited to the current project or profile. `--output` must remain inside the repository.
---
title: Security contract
description: Manifest trust, secret handling, local exposure, and ownership.
---

- Every DevFn manifest can declare lifecycle commands, so the CLI refuses to load JSON, TypeScript, or JavaScript until the user records trust for its exact digest with `--trust`. JSON is parsed directly from the verified bytes; executable manifests run from a private copy of those same bytes and must be self-contained, with imports and `require()` rejected so dependency files cannot bypass the digest boundary.
- Runtime children inherit a small base environment plus explicit `envAllowlist` entries. Sensitive-looking keys must also be listed in `secretEnv`; a detached wrapper redacts those effective values before native-process logs are persisted. Literal values are rejected only when their key looks sensitive, so review every manifest literal. Compose logging is disabled for services with `secretEnv` because Docker otherwise retains historical unredacted logs. Secrets are not persisted in the registry or lifecycle receipt.
- Generated environment and state files use owner-only modes (default `0600`); their directories use `0700`. Existing files are explicitly re-permissioned after each write.
- Local ports and proxy targets bind to loopback unless a manifest explicitly selects public exposure. Profiles containing public processes or ports require the separate `--allow-public` confirmation on every start. A public Cloudflare tunnel must never be inferred.
- Repository-relative process, Compose, runtime, policy, and output paths are validated against lexical and symlink path escape.
- PID ownership uses a birth signature where the host exposes one. DevFn refuses to stop a reused PID.
- `down` stops only the exact worktree instance. Ordinary shutdown removes no persistent Docker volumes.
- Project hostnames must be concrete `.localhost` names. DevFn manages only a Caddy process it started itself and refuses to overwrite an unrelated Caddy admin endpoint.
- Volume deletion, database reset, public tunnels, and other destructive operations are outside ordinary lifecycle commands and require separate explicit tooling and confirmation.
---
title: Lifecycle and diagnostics
description: Start, inspect, stop, and recover one worktree instance.
---

`devfn up` plans resources in dependency order, reserves ports before mutation, starts selected native processes and Compose services, verifies readiness, registers proxy routes, and returns a machine-readable receipt. If an invocation fails, rollback targets resources created by that invocation. `status`, `logs`, and `doctor` expose live state and diagnostics; `down` stops only the exact worktree instance.

There is no background daemon in version 0.1. State, journals, logs, and generated environment files are kept under the configured runtime directory, `.devfn/` by default. Process ownership uses a PID birth signature where the host supplies one, so cleanup refuses a reused PID.

Ordinary `down` does not delete persistent Docker volumes. It is also not a general reset command. Explicit configured environment outputs may have overwritten files that existed before adoption; inspect them before manual cleanup. The [core package](/docs/reference/core), [process supervisor](/docs/reference/processes), and [migration guide](/docs/reference/migration) describe lifecycle boundaries.
# Shared DocsFn site runtime

The per-function sites supply their config and Vite raw-content globs to `createDocsSiteRuntime`. Each factory call owns its own manifest/search/compiled-content cache. Keep this module server-only; layout loaders return only site/navigation metadata, and search is loaded from `/search.json` when needed.

`Search.svelte` uses DocsFn's search runtime with a native modal dialog. It supports the visible trigger, Ctrl/Cmd+K, Escape, keyboard-focusable result links, loading state, and errors without the published UI dialog's SSR limitation.

Each site resolves the shared module's DocsFn imports through its own Vite aliases so it uses the versions pinned by that site. Run `npm run build` in the affected `<function>/docs` directory. After changing shared code, build all consumers and verify desktop search (including a result navigation and Escape) plus the mobile Menu drawer. Keep the responsive open-drawer override when using the current published theme.

The new-site PRs carry identical copies of this shared directory so they can land independently. Once merged, edits belong here rather than in the small per-site factory wrappers.

parseFrontmatter only recognizes frontmatter when the file starts with exactly "---\n" (LF, no BOM), and it scans for "\n---" without allowing CRLF before the closing fence. a markdown file with CRLF line endings or a BOM has its frontmatter treated as page body, so the title/description leak visibly into rendered docs pages and llms.txt artifacts. match /^---\r?\n/ for the opening fence and /\r?\n---(\r?\n|$)/ for the closing fence.

if (!/^---\r?\n/.test(source)) {
    return { body: source, frontmatter: {} };
  }

  const closingIndex = source.search(/\r?\n---(\r?\n|$)/, );
```

    return { body: source, frontmatter: {} };
  }

  const closingIndex = source.search(/\r?\n---(\r?\n|$)/, );
```

Add a database adapter, e.g. `db: memoryAdapter()` from `@superfunctions/db/adapters/memory`, matching the setup shown in docs/content/docs/quickstart/nextjs.md.



 5  filefn/docs/content/docs/recipes/video-uploads.md 46 


P2: This example now emits only a 720p transcode, while the page Goal (`- 720p and 480p transcodes for adaptive playback.`) and the header (`multi-resolution transcoding`) still promise a 480p rendition. Fix the mismatch by updating the Goal/header to a single 720p transcode, or register a second processor instance for 480p (different artifact storage keys) as adapters/processors.md recommends.



 6  filefn/docs/content/docs/adapters/storage-gcs.md 24 


P2: This adapter advertises `signedUploadUrls: true` and implements `signUploadUrl`/`signDownloadUrl` (packages/storage-gcs/src/adapter.ts), so the claim that "signed upload URLs are not advertised" is incorrect and will mislead users into avoiding the available signed-upload path. Only the multipart claim is accurate: `multipart: false`. Reword to state that native multipart is not advertised while signed upload/download URLs are.



 7  filefn/docs/content/docs/adapters/db-sqlite.md 20 


P2: The copied SQLite snippet omits the Drizzle schema, so `drizzleAdapter` throws at runtime. `packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/index.ts` requires `db._.fullSchema` and raises "You must pass schema to drizzle() constructor: drizzle(client, { schema })" when it is missing. Showing `drizzle(sqlite)` without the schema makes the sample fail on first table resolution. Pass the generated schema (`drizzle(sqlite, { schema })`) or add a note pointing at `superfunctions generate-schema`, and keep the `schema` in the constructor, not only the migration step.



 8  filefn/docs/content/docs/frameworks/hono.md 21 


P2: This example calls `drizzle(pool)` without a schema, but `drizzleAdapter` resolves tables from Drizzle's schema registry (`db._.fullSchema`) and throws `drizzleAdapter: No schema found in Drizzle instance. You must pass schema to drizzle() constructor` whenever filefn/authfn resolves a model (packages/db/src/adapters/drizzle/index.ts:144-152). As written, the snippet fails at runtime. Generate the filefn (and authfn) schema with `@superfunctions/cli generate-schema` and pass it to `drizzle(pool, { schema })`, matching the authfn Drizzle docs, which state the adapter "cannot operate without it."



 9  filefn/docs/content/docs/quickstart/express.md 43 


P2: `fileFn.router.handle()` is typed to return `Promise<Response | null>` and returns `null` when no route matches (filefn/server/src/router.ts). The old snippet guarded that case and responded 404; `toExpress` instead calls `webResponse.status` on the result of `router.handle(...)`, so with `null` it throws a TypeError and Express falls into the default error handler with a 500. Requests to unmatched paths under `/filefn` now get 500 instead of 404, and the snippet only works if the app adds an error handler. Either make the http-express adapter treat a null/undefined handle result as a 404, or keep a null check in the snippet.



 10  filefn/docs/content/docs/frameworks/bun.md 20 


P2: `drizzle(sqlite)` is created without a schema, but `drizzleAdapter` resolves every table from `db._.fullSchema` and throws "No schema found in Drizzle instance" on the first CRUD operation. Pass the generated schema: `drizzle(sqlite, { schema })`, as the production example does in filefn/examples/production/server/src/db.ts.

P2: The updated `stripExif` sample no longer performs any metadata-stripping step. The actual processor API (`filefn/processing/src/processors/image-transform.ts`) supports only `resize | crop | rotate` operations, and the sample's single `resize` + JPEG re-encode only drops EXIF incidentally (via sharp's default `withMetadata` behaviour) — nothing in the sample states that, and the processor name plus the page's goal bullet ("EXIF metadata stripped to avoid leaking GPS coordinates") and the "EXIF and privacy" section (`createImageTransformProcessor` with `strip-metadata`) still promise explicit stripping. `strip-metadata` is not a valid operation anywhere in the package (only referenced in this page's text and llms-full.txt), so the recipe now contradicts both the library API and its own narrative. Rename the processor to reflect what it does (e.g. `normalise`), state in the sample that the JPEG re-encode discards EXIF, and update the "EXIF and privacy" section so it doesn't recommend the nonexistent `strip-metadata` option. Note also that `intent: "full"`/`"download"` resolve to the original file bytes (service.ts `options.intent === 'full'` returns `originalDescriptor()`), so the EXIF guarantee only holds for apps that consume the `normalised`/thumbnail artifacts, never for full/detail rendering.

P3: The example comment tells readers to pass `createFileFn({ db, storage, ... })`, but `FileFnConfig.db` is marked `@deprecated Use database` in `filefn/server/src/index.ts`. Recommend the non-deprecated `database` key so the docs don't steer new integrations toward the deprecated option.

Constructing Drizzle as `drizzle(pool)` leaves `db._.fullSchema` unavailable, but `drizzleAdapter` resolves every model through that registry and throws before the first database operation when no schema was supplied. The PostgreSQL, SQLite, Hono, and Bun examples added here therefore cannot serve a FileFn request even after the SQL tables are provisioned; generate/import the Drizzle table definitions and construct the client with `drizzle(..., { schema })`.

## Resources and actions

The capability covers files, versions, upload sessions, grants, share links, policies, and processing artifacts. Child resources such as versions, grants, shares, and artifacts are listed under an authorized file. Operations include authorized downloads, file deletion, upload creation/completion/abort, grant and share creation/revocation, and artifact processing.

File deletion requires MFA confirmation and removes the file's versions, artifacts, grants, and shares. Other writes carry their own risk and confirmation metadata; the host must enforce the capability's declared policy and write audit records. Upload tokens, storage keys, share tokens, provider URLs and headers, and policy storage paths are sensitive and must not leak through list responses.

For an admin download, the domain service requires a signed URL or same-origin proxy descriptor. It rejects provider request headers instead of exposing them to a browser. Review [downloads](/docs/features/downloads), [grants](/docs/features/grants), and [share links](/docs/features/share-links) for the underlying FileFn access rules.

The [capability source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/filefn/admin/src/index.ts) defines operation IDs and schemas. The [domain service](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/filefn/admin/src/domain-service.ts) shows how the public FileFn facade enforces ownership and creates safe responses.

The admin service itself only rejects descriptors with non-empty provider headers; it does not validate a URL’s origin or signature. Hosts using custom storage/download services must ensure that every returned header-free URL is safe for the intended client and authorization scope.

For hosts using a custom `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`, the linked pages do not describe operator policies: they document the CLI's remote lock files, automatic rollback implementation, and `.env` layout. `HostFnOperatorService` merely delegates deploy, rollback, and variable effects to the executor, so none of those behaviors is inherited automatically. Calling these the corresponding operator policies can lead control-plane integrators to rely on concurrency and recovery guarantees they do not have; identify them as CLI-only examples or state which behavior the executor must implement.

Anyone following this reference to exercise the documented source may install an unrelated or stale registry artifact; either omit these lines or clearly separate them from the TypeScript adoption documented by this site.

 1  langfn/docs/content/docs/operations-and-limits.md 10 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop claiming the release gate runs duplication checks**

The documented gate does not perform a duplication check: `scripts/gate-langfn-release.mjs` only runs the Turbo build, TypeScript typecheck, test suite, and built-module imports.  2  langfn/docs/src/routes/+layout.server.ts 13 ![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Performance](https://img.shields.io/badge/Performance-FF6D00) ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-medium-1A7BBE)


The layout server load returns the entire DocsSiteSource object — the full manifest (including every page's markdown `body`, since manifest.pages[].body is populated by the bundled provider) plus the full search artifact — as layout data that SvelteKit serializes into the client payload for every page render. Every docs page navigation downloads a duplicated copy of all documentation bodies and the search index, inflating each HTML/data response by the size of the whole site. Return only the fields the layout template actually uses (config.navigation, config.site, siteTitle, canonicalUrl) and fetch the rest via the dedicated server endpoints (e.g. /search.json) or per-route load functions.

```typescript
export const load: LayoutServerLoad = async () => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();
  return {
    source: {
      siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
      canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
      config: source.config,
    },
  };
};
```

 28  langfn/docs/content/docs/http.md 12 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Qualify SSE cancellation by adapter support**

In the documented Express setup below, this guarantee does not hold: `packages/http-express/src/adapter.ts` creates the Web `Request` without wiring `req` disconnects to its signal, and `convertToExpressResponse` buffers the entire body with `webResponse.text()`. Consequently, callers using exactly the recommended `toExpress(router)` mount neither receive incremental SSE nor cancel model work on disconnect; qualify this statement or recommend an adapter that propagates streaming and disconnect signals.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

 29  langfn/docs/content/docs/http.md 50 Mounting through `toExpress(router)` does not support the `/stream` SSE behavior this guide advertises: the current Express adapter waits for `webResponse.text()` to finish before sending anything, and its converted `Request` is not aborted on client disconnect. A consumer using this server for `/stream` will see no live events, and disconnecting will not cancel model work.
