 0  mailfn/docs/src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts 65 ![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Bug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bug-B71C1C) ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-medium-1A7BBE)


The api-route surface hardcodes `sidebarId: "api"`, but docsfn.config.ts defines only the `docs` sidebar, so `source.manifest.sidebars[sidebarId]` is undefined for api pages. any future API-reference page (content/api) will render through DocsLayout with no sidebar/navigation, breaking the documented package-reference navigation. use `"docs"` (the configured sidebar key) or add an `api` sidebar to docsfn.config.ts.







 1  mailfn/docs/content/docs/testing.md 18 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Capture the wait boundary before triggering the workflow**

When a user replaces the preceding comment with an awaited product invocation, a fast email can be accepted before this timestamp is captured; `waitForMessages` maps `after` to the strict `receivedAfter` filter, so that message is excluded and the example intermittently times out. Capture the timestamp before triggering the workflow and pass that saved value to `waitForOtp`; the duplicated example in `reference/testing.md` should be corrected as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

 2  mailfn/docs/svelte.config.js 17 ![kody code-review](https://img.shields.io/badge/kody-code--review-312B4B?labelColor=C9BBF2) ![Bug](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bug-B71C1C) ![medium](https://img.shields.io/badge/severity_level-medium-1A7BBE)


`appDir: "docs/_app"` sets a multi-segment path containing '/', but SvelteKit validates `kit.appDir` as a single directory name and hard-errors on config validation. whenever CLOUDFLARE_DOCS_DEPLOY=1 (the exact deploy mode this branch implements), `vite build`/`vite dev` fail with a config validation error, so the Cloudflare deployment path cannot build. use a single-segment name (e.g. `_app` or `_docs_app`) and express any path prefix via `paths.base`/`paths.assets` instead.







 3  mailfn/docs/package.json 18 **Security issue**  
🛑 Blocker — must fix before merge

**Known vulnerabilities in svelte@5.0.0**

OSV.dev reports 6 known vulnerabilities affecting `svelte@5.0.0`, introduced by this PR:

- [GHSA-crpf-4hrx-3jrp](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27125) **moderate**: Svelte SSR attribute spreading includes inherited properties from prototype chain — fixed in 5.51.5
- [GHSA-f7gr-6p89-r883](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27121) **moderate**: Svelte affected by cross-site scripting via spread attributes in Svelte SSR — fixed in 5.51.5
- [GHSA-m56q-vw4c-c2cp](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-27122) **moderate**: Svelte SSR does not validate dynamic element tag names in `<svelte:element>` — fixed in 5.51.5

…and 3 more — see the OSV links above.

Upgrade to 5.51.5 or later.

---



 4  mailfn/docs/package.json 8 **Configuration**  
⚠️ Warning

**test script uses vitest which is not a declared dependency**

The `test` script runs `vitest run --passWithNoTests`, but `vitest` does not appear in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`. It currently only resolves via hoisting from the monorepo root `devDependencies`, which breaks under isolated installs (e.g. a clean workspace install or a package-manager with strict dependency rules) and makes the script fail with a command-not-found. Other packages in this monorepo that use vitest (e.g. `apifn/docsfn`, `authfn/api-keys`) declare `"vitest": "^3.2.4"` in `devDependencies`. Add it here for a self-contained package.

```suggestion
"test": "vitest run --passWithNoTests",
    "typecheck": "svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json",
```

---



 5  mailfn/docs/content/docs/reference/testing.md 18 


P2: Capture the wait boundary before triggering the workflow and pass that saved timestamp as `after`; otherwise a fast message can fall outside the strict receive-time filter. Apply the same correction to the reference example.



 6  mailfn/docs/tsconfig.json 2 


P2: Extending `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json` while also overriding `include`/`types`/`lib`/`target` cancels the generated config: the child `include` replaces the generated program entries (`.svelte-kit/ambient.d.ts`, `.svelte-kit/types/**/*.d.ts`), so `$app/*`, `$env/*`, and `$types` ambient declarations disappear from typechecks and the IDE. Since `/.svelte-kit` is gitignored, a fresh checkout also has no base file until `svelte-kit sync` (dev/build) runs. Match the repo's other SvelteKit apps (`filefn/examples/full-demo/client`, `uifn/catalogs/svelte`, `superconsole`): extend only with a minimal `compilerOptions` and no `include`/`types` overrides — or, like the sibling `authfn/docs`, keep this standalone config and drop the `extends` line.



 7  mailfn/docs/src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.svelte 2 


P2: These components are imported from `@docsfn/svelte` package-root subpaths (`@docsfn/svelte/DocsContent.svelte`, etc.), but the only other DocsFn consumer in this repo (authfn/docs, same pinned `@docsfn/svelte` 0.0.3) imports every one of these components through `@site/*` aliases defined in `vite.config.ts` that resolve into the package's `src/` directory. The alias indirection exists because the published package's component files are not resolvable at the package root. Mirror the authfn/docs pattern: add the `@site/*` aliases to `vite.config.ts` and import via those aliases here, in `+layout.svelte`, and in `DocsSiteSearch.svelte`, or confirm the direct subpaths resolve in a clean lockfile install. As-is, a fresh CI node_modules resolution of these imports can fail even though local authoring builds passed.



 8  mailfn/docs/package.json 29 


P2: Raise the Svelte version floor to 5.51.5 or later; `^5.0.0` still permits releases with the reported SSR vulnerabilities.



 9  mailfn/docs/src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts 65 


P2: Use the configured `docs` sidebar or add an `api` sidebar; API-reference routes currently resolve this key to `undefined` and lose the package navigation.



 10  mailfn/docs/content/docs/cloudflare-runtime.md 14 


P3: The sample's `createSendFnAdapter` is exported from `@mailfn/sendfn`, not `@mailfn/cloudflare`, and it composes via the `sendAdapter` option rather than as a bare entry in the handlers object. A reader copying this snippet has no correct path to wire it. Show the import and the `sendAdapter` field, or drop the composition hint.



 11  mailfn/docs/static/llms-full.txt 12 


P3: Every page section in this file repeats its title: DocsFn prepends `# <title>` + the description blockquote, and then the source page body starts with the same `# <title>` again (e.g. `# Administration capability` appears at the top and again right after the description). This duplication across all 25 sections wastes tokens in a single-shot LLM file and adds no information. Remove the in-body H1 from the source pages in `mailfn/docs/content/docs/**` (which the generator prepends itself) or configure the generator not to prepend the title when the body already starts with it.



 12  mailfn/docs/static/llms-full.txt 7 


P3: The intro claims a "structured manifest" is emitted alongside this file, but the generation script writes only `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` and no manifest artifact exists anywhere in `mailfn/docs` (the DocsFn manifest is built only in memory by `docs-site-source.ts`; the only JSON route is `search.json`). LLM consumers told to prefer a non-existent manifest will look for a file that is never produced. Either emit a manifest (e.g., write `buildManifest` output as JSON in `scripts/generate-llms.mjs`) or reword the sentence to reference the MCP server / search index only.



 13  mailfn/docs/content/docs/reference/cli.md 18 


P3: The command list omits `message attachments`, which the CLI actually supports (`message:attachments` → `client.listAttachments`, and CLI `help()` lists `message list|read|attachments|wait|extract`). Readers of this reference page will miss that the CLI can list attachments. Add `attachments` to the coverage sentence (and keep the source README in sync).



 14  mailfn/docs/package.json 10 


P3: Declare Vitest in this workspace's `devDependencies`; isolated installs cannot resolve the executable invoked by this script.



 15 OUTDATED mailfn/docs/src/lib/components/DocsSiteSearch.svelte None The shared Cloudflare docs routing only forwards `/docs*` to a product Worker, so a browser request to `/search.json` will miss this site even after MailFn is registered. The checked-in `llms*.txt` assets have the same root-path problem; expose these endpoints under the mounted path (or explicitly route their root paths) before hosting it there.



 16  mailfn/docs/content/docs/cli-and-mcp.md 11 This inline `MAILFN_URL=... MAILFN_TOKEN=...` assignment only applies to `inbox create`; the next two commands fail because the CLI requires both values on every invocation. The create output also hides the returned inbox credential by default, so show how to reveal it intentionally and pass that scoped token to the subsequent commands (and update the repeated reference example).

 17  scripts/docs-site/runtime.ts 509 


P2: This parser does not preserve standard DocsFn/YAML frontmatter: arrays, nested values, multiline fields, and scalar types are converted into incorrect strings. Use the same YAML/frontmatter parser as DocsFn instead of reimplementing metadata parsing, otherwise adding valid document metadata silently produces incorrect routes, navigation, or search metadata.



 18  mailfn/docs/vite.config.ts 22 


P2: These aliases apply to every import of `@docsfn/core` in the module graph, including imports inside `@docsfn/svelte@0.0.3`. The lockfile installs `@docsfn/svelte@0.0.3` with a nested `mailfn/docs/node_modules/@docsfn/svelte/node_modules/@docsfn/core@0.0.3` because svelte 0.0.3 pins core `0.0.3`, while the site pins core `0.0.5`. Redirecting svelte's internal imports to 0.0.5 overrides that declared dependency contract; any API drift between core 0.0.3 and 0.0.5 in the APIs svelte uses would surface only at runtime, since the SSR routes in `src/routes/docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts` execute on the edge rather than during `vite build`. Align the declared versions in `mailfn/docs/package.json` (e.g. upgrade `@docsfn/svelte` to a version that pairs with core 0.0.5, or pin the site's core to 0.0.3) instead of silently aliasing over the mismatch.



 19  mailfn/docs/content/docs/testing.md 25 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  State that verification waits throw on timeout**

When no matching message arrives, `waitForOtp` and `waitForVerificationLink` do not expose timeout as normal result-based control flow: `mailfn/testing/src/index.ts` immediately throws `MailFnAssertionError`. Consumers following this guidance may attempt to inspect a result that is never returned and leave expected timeouts unhandled. Document the assertion behavior or direct callers that need a timeout result to `client.waitForMessages`; the same incorrect claim also appears in `content/docs/reference/testing.md`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

 20  mailfn/docs/content/docs/reference/client.md 21 **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Describe the attachment download wrapper accurately**

For consumers calling `downloadAttachment`, the return value is not a `Uint8Array`; `mailfn/client/src/client.ts` returns `{ attachment: AttachmentDescriptor, data: Uint8Array }`. This wording can cause JavaScript users to pass the wrapper itself to byte-processing APIs instead of its `data` field. Clarify that only `readRaw` returns bytes directly and that attachment bytes are in `result.data`; the same inaccurate statement appears in `content/docs/messages-and-evidence.md`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The route files `+layout.server.ts`, `docs/[...slug]/+page.server.ts`, and `search.json/+server.ts` import `./$types`, and `+layout.svelte` imports `$app/stores`, so editors and `svelte-check` will report “Cannot find module” for these until the generated files are re-added (vite build passes because it runs no tsc step). Copy the generated-file entries into `include`; the `lib` override also drops `DOM.Iterable` from the base config — keep it if any DOM collections are iterated.


sendfn/docs/src/routes/+page.server.ts 


P3: This file is a runtime no-op: SvelteKit already merges the layout's `source` into the page's `data`, so `return parent()` adds nothing, and it defeats its stated purpose — the bare `PageServerLoad` annotation widens the page's `PageData` to `Record<string, any>`, leaving `data.source` untyped in `+page.svelte`. Delete the file (the generated `PageData` keeps the layout's typed `source`), or, if kept, type the generic explicitly: `PageServerLoad<{ source: DocsSiteSource }>`.


sendfn/docs/src/routes/+page.svelte 


P3: This landing page is a near-verbatim copy of authfn/docs/src/routes/+page.svelte and filefn/docs/src/routes/+page.svelte: the hero, features grid, quick-link cards, and the whole ~200-line `<style>` block are identical except for the five content constants (tagline, features, quickLinks, h1, meta blurb). This is the third consumer site carrying the same template, so style/layout fixes now have to be applied three times. Consider extracting a shared `LandingPage` component and writing each site's page as content-props only.


scripts/docs-site/runtime.ts 


P1: Cloudflare builds can’t rely on `node:path` unless the worker enables Node.js compatibility; this shared runtime is imported by the Cloudflare-deployable SendFn site. Replace the Node path dependency with platform-neutral POSIX path helpers, or explicitly enable `nodejs_compat` for every Cloudflare deployment.


sendfn/docs/vite.config.ts 


P2: These aliases call synchronous `import.meta.resolve` at config load, which is only unflagged on Node >= 20.6. The repo declares engines `node >=18.17.0` and CI runs a Node 18.20.8 job; on Node 18 the call is undefined, so `fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve(...))` throws a TypeError and `vite dev`/`vite build` for @sendfn/docs fails before Vite starts. The aliases are also redundant identity mappings: `import.meta.resolve("@docsfn/core")` resolves to the same entry Vite already resolves from the nearest `node_modules`, so the simplest fix is to delete these two entries (plus the comment) — sibling docs sites (filefn/docs, authfn/docs) alias neither `@docsfn/core` nor its subpath and rely on `noExternal` for the transform. scripts/docs-site/README.md 


P3: The final paragraph describes new-site PRs "carrying identical copies of this shared directory" so they can land independently, but this PR's site does not vendor a copy: sendfn/docs/src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts and sendfn/docs/src/lib/components/DocsSiteSearch.svelte both import the shared module via repo-relative `../../../../../scripts/docs-site/...` paths, and no copy exists under sendfn/docs. In this monorepo every function's docs site resolves to the single canonical `scripts/docs-site/`, so copies landing at the same path would conflict rather than land independently. Reword to describe the actual pattern: site PRs include this shared directory as part of the same change (referencing it from scripts/docs-site), and after merge edits belong here.

Search then fails even though the `/search.json` SvelteKit endpoint works locally. Serve the search artifact under the routed prefix and request that URL, or explicitly route the root endpoint to this Worker.

      const provider = createBundledContentProvider(config);

          canonicalUrl: config.site.canonicalUrl,
          compatPreset,
          config,
        },
        compiledCache,

import { getTopNavigation, resolveMarkdownRelativeLinks, type Sidebar } from "@docsfn/core";

  type SvelteDocsPageSurface,
} from "@docsfn/sveltekit";
import { getCompiledDocsPage, loadDocsSiteSource } from "$lib/server/docs-site-source";
import type { PageServerLoad } from "./$types";

function buildCanonicalUrl(canonicalBase: string | undefined, path: string): string {
  if (!canonicalBase) {
    return path;
  }
  let end = canonicalBase.length;
  while (end > 0 && canonicalBase[end - 1] === "/") end--;
  const origin = canonicalBase.slice(0, end);
  const normalizedPath = path.startsWith("/") ? path : `/${path}`;
  return `${origin}${normalizedPath}`;
}

function isRouteNotFoundError(input: unknown): input is { message: string } {
  return (
    typeof input === "object" &&
    input !== null &&
    "code" in input &&
    input.code === "DOCS_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND" &&
    "message" in input &&
    typeof input.message === "string"
  );
}

function hasNestedDocsRoutes(routes: Record<string, string>, route: string): boolean {
  return Object.keys(routes).some((candidate) => candidate.startsWith(`${route}/`));
}

export const load: PageServerLoad = async ({ params }) => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();

  let routeEntry;
  try {
    routeEntry = resolveDocsRouteDataOrThrow(params.slug, source.manifest, {
      basePath: "/docs",
    });
  } catch (routeError) {
    if (isRouteNotFoundError(routeError)) {
      throw error(404, routeError.message);
    }
    throw routeError;
  }

  if (routeEntry.kind === "post") {
    throw error(404, `unsupported docs route kind: ${routeEntry.kind}`);
  }

  let surface: SvelteDocsPageSurface;
  if (routeEntry.kind === "api") {
    const api = routeEntry.api;
    const route = routeEntry.route;
    surface = {
      route,
      title: api.title,
      description:
        typeof api.frontmatter.description === "string" ? api.frontmatter.description : undefined,
      canonicalPath: route,
      canonicalUrl: buildCanonicalUrl(source.canonicalUrl, route),
      sidebarId: "api",
      headings: [],
      breadcrumbs: [
        { label: "Docs", href: "/docs" },
        { label: "Package reference", href: "/docs/reference" },
        { label: api.title, href: route },
      ],
      pagination: {},
      topNav: getTopNavigation(source.manifest),
      versions: source.manifest.versions,
    };
  } else {
    surface = resolveDocsPageSurface({
      manifest: source.manifest,
      route: routeEntry.route,
      page: routeEntry.page,
      options: {
        basePath: "/docs",
        homeHref: "/docs",
        canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
        versionMode: "path-prefix",
      },
    });
  }

  const sidebarId = surface.sidebarId ?? "default";
  const sidebar: Sidebar | undefined = source.manifest.sidebars[sidebarId];

  const compiled =
    routeEntry.kind === "page"
      ? resolveMarkdownRelativeLinks({
          compiled: await getCompiledDocsPage(routeEntry.page.id),
          route: routeEntry.route,
          sourcePath: routeEntry.page.id.replace(/^docs:/, ""),
          isIndexRoute: hasNestedDocsRoutes(source.manifest.routes, routeEntry.route),
        })
      : undefined;

  return {
    routeEntry,
    surface,
    sidebar,
    compiled,
    siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
  };
};

`serverStatePromise` is assigned before the async body settles. If `buildManifest`, `buildSearchIndex`, or any content-provider step rejects once, the rejection is cached in the module-level variable forever — every subsequent request to any route keeps returning that rejected promise and the site serves 500s until the server process restarts. ```suggestion
async function loadDocsSiteServerState(): Promise<DocsSiteServerState> {
  if (!serverStatePromise) {
    const promise = (async () => {
      const siteRoot = ".";
      const config = docsConfig satisfies DocsConfig;
      const provider = createBundledContentProvider(config);
      const manifest = await buildManifest(provider, config);
      const searchArtifact = await buildSearchIndex(manifest, {
        search: config.search,
        auth: config.auth,
      });
      const compatPreset = config.compat?.preset ?? "none";
      const compiledCache = createCompiledCache({
        manifest,
        compatPreset,
      });

      return {
        source: {
          siteRoot,
          manifest,
          searchArtifact,
          siteTitle: config.site.title,
          canonicalUrl: config.site.canonicalUrl,
          compatPreset,
          config,
        },
        compiledCache,
      };
    })();
    promise.catch(() => {
      if (serverStatePromise === promise) {
        serverStatePromise = null;
      }
    });
    serverStatePromise = promise;
  }

import { getTopNavigation, resolveMarkdownRelativeLinks, type Sidebar } from "@docsfn/core";
import {
  resolveDocsPageSurface,

  type SvelteDocsPageSurface,
} from "@docsfn/sveltekit";
import { getCompiledDocsPage, loadDocsSiteSource } from "$lib/server/docs-site-source";
import type { PageServerLoad } from "./$types";

function buildCanonicalUrl(canonicalBase: string | undefined, path: string): string {
  if (!canonicalBase) {
    return path;
  }
  let end = canonicalBase.length;
  while (end > 0 && canonicalBase[end - 1] === "/") end--;
  const origin = canonicalBase.slice(0, end);
  const normalizedPath = path.startsWith("/") ? path : `/${path}`;
  return `${origin}${normalizedPath}`;
}

function isRouteNotFoundError(input: unknown): input is { message: string } {
  return (
    typeof input === "object" &&
    input !== null &&
    "code" in input &&
    input.code === "DOCS_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND" &&
    "message" in input &&
    typeof input.message === "string"
  );
}

function hasNestedDocsRoutes(routes: Record<string, string>, route: string): boolean {
  return Object.keys(routes).some((candidate) => candidate.startsWith(`${route}/`));
}

export const load: PageServerLoad = async ({ params }) => {
  const source = await loadDocsSiteSource();

  let routeEntry;
  try {
    routeEntry = resolveDocsRouteDataOrThrow(params.slug, source.manifest, {
      basePath: "/docs",
    });
  } catch (routeError) {
    if (isRouteNotFoundError(routeError)) {
      throw error(404, routeError.message);
    }
    throw routeError;
  }

  if (routeEntry.kind === "post") {
    throw error(404, `unsupported docs route kind: ${routeEntry.kind}`);
  }

  let surface: SvelteDocsPageSurface;
  if (routeEntry.kind === "api") {
    const api = routeEntry.api;
    const route = routeEntry.route;
    surface = {
      route,
      title: api.title,
      description:
        typeof api.frontmatter.description === "string" ? api.frontmatter.description : undefined,
      canonicalPath: route,
      canonicalUrl: buildCanonicalUrl(source.canonicalUrl, route),
      sidebarId: "api",
      headings: [],
      breadcrumbs: [
        { label: "Docs", href: "/docs" },
        { label: "Package reference", href: "/docs/reference" },
        { label: api.title, href: route },
      ],
      pagination: {},
      topNav: getTopNavigation(source.manifest),
      versions: source.manifest.versions,
    };
  } else {
    surface = resolveDocsPageSurface({
      manifest: source.manifest,
      route: routeEntry.route,
      page: routeEntry.page,
      options: {
        basePath: "/docs",
        homeHref: "/docs",
        canonicalUrl: source.canonicalUrl,
        versionMode: "path-prefix",
      },
    });
  }

  const sidebarId = surface.sidebarId ?? "default";
  const sidebar: Sidebar | undefined = source.manifest.sidebars[sidebarId];

  const compiled =
    routeEntry.kind === "page"
      ? resolveMarkdownRelativeLinks({
          compiled: await getCompiledDocsPage(routeEntry.page.id),
          route: routeEntry.route,
          sourcePath: routeEntry.page.id.replace(/^docs:/, ""),
          isIndexRoute: hasNestedDocsRoutes(source.manifest.routes, routeEntry.route),
        })
      : undefined;

  return {
    routeEntry,
    surface,
    sidebar,
    compiled,
    siteTitle: source.siteTitle,
  };
};

**Rejected initialization promise is cached forever**

`serverStatePromise` is assigned before the async body settles. If `buildManifest`, `buildSearchIndex`, or any content-provider step rejects once, the rejection is cached in the module-level variable forever — every subsequent request to any route keeps returning that rejected promise and the site serves 500s until the server process restarts. Reset the variable on failure so a transient error retries instead of bricking the server.

```suggestion
async function loadDocsSiteServerState(): Promise<DocsSiteServerState> {
  if (!serverStatePromise) {
    const promise = (async () => {
      const siteRoot = ".";
      const config = docsConfig satisfies DocsConfig;
      const provider = createBundledContentProvider(config);
      const manifest = await buildManifest(provider, config);
      const searchArtifact = await buildSearchIndex(manifest, {
        search: config.search,
        auth: config.auth,
      });
      const compatPreset = config.compat?.preset ?? "none";
      const compiledCache = createCompiledCache({
        manifest,
        compatPreset,
      });

      return {
        source: {
          siteRoot,
          manifest,
          searchArtifact,
          siteTitle: config.site.title,
          canonicalUrl: config.site.canonicalUrl,
          compatPreset,
          config,
        },
        compiledCache,
      };
    })();
    promise.catch(() => {
      if (serverStatePromise === promise) {
        serverStatePromise = null;
      }
    });
    serverStatePromise = promise;
  }

  return serverStatePromise;
}

function buildCanonicalUrl(canonicalBase: string | undefined, path: string): string {
  if (!canonicalBase) {
    return path;
  }
  let end = canonicalBase.length;
  while (end > 0 && canonicalBase[end - 1] === "/") end--;
  const origin = canonicalBase.slice(0, end);
  const normalizedPath = path.startsWith("/") ? path : `/${path}`;
  return `${origin}${normalizedPath}`;
}

function isRouteNotFoundError(input: unknown): input is { message: string } {

    input !== null &&
    "code" in input &&
    input.code === "DOCS_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND" &&
    "message" in input &&
    typeof input.message === "string"
  );
}

function hasNestedDocsRoutes(routes: Record<string, string>, route: string): boolean {
  return Object.keys(routes).some((candidate) => candidate.startsWith(`${route}/`));

        versionMode: "path-prefix",

 13  mdfn/docs/src/routes/+layout.server.ts None 


P2: Keep `manifest` and `searchArtifact` out of layout data; SvelteKit serializes server-load results into each SSR/hydration response, shipping all page bodies and the search index. Return only layout-rendered fields and access these artifacts through server helpers in route and search loads.



 14  mdfn/docs/src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts None 


P2: Restrict this eager raw glob to the text artifacts the provider needs; adding images or fonts under `static/` otherwise embeds their contents in the server bundle as strings.



 15  mdfn/docs/package.json 22 


P3: The README's bare `docsfn validate --root .` command fails in a clean checkout because this local CLI is only added to `PATH` by npm scripts. Add a `validate` script and invoke it with `npm run validate`.



 16  mdfn/docs/src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts None 


P3: This file duplicates the full 500-line site-source implementation already present in the authfn and filefn docs sites. Extract the shared provider and cache logic into a reusable module so fixes and behavior changes do not need to be maintained in three copies.



 17  mdfn/docs/content/docs/reference/meta.json 21 


P3: `overview` is listed 18th (after `markdown`) even though it is the umbrella overview that `index.md` leads with ("The overview explains the product guarantees"). In the rendered sidebar it appears buried mid-list. Moving it directly after `index` makes the navigation reflect its role as the entry point for the section.

item.stdout:
Every operation requires an explicit tenant ID and tag array. All supplied tags must match; an empty array selects the entire explicit tenant. Tags are retrieval filters, not membership or sharing authority. Model-extracted tags are stored as descriptive metadata and cannot expand the caller's container tags.

`update({ tenantId, containerTags, id, expectedRevision, content })` uses compare-and-update and replaces the embedding. Failed re-embedding leaves the prior revision intact. `forget({ tenantId, containerTags, id, expectedRevision? })` scrubs content, vector and metadata, removes relationships and retains an immutable-ID tombstone. Concurrent stale updates cannot resurrect a tombstone. Forget can be retried; Postgres performs scrubbing and relationship cleanup in one transaction. A failed transaction reports failure and can be retried.

The application must deny retrieval as soon as its authoritative the authoritative application store record is forgotten, including while derived-store cleanup is pending. MemoryFn cannot infer the state of an external source of authority. Results must be intersected with current The application permissions and authoritative deletion state. External indexes and replicas require equivalent tombstone checks and retryable cleanup; this package's Postgres vector lives in the same row as the tombstone.

The HTTP router requires an `authorize(request)` callback returning trusted scope or null. Request bodies cannot choose a tenant. The MCP adapter requires a trusted scope at construction; instantiate it per authorized scope and revoke access at the host boundary.


---

The assets glob eagerly raw-imports every file under static/** as UTF-8 strings, so any binary asset (images, fonts) added to static/ gets inlined as a mangled string on every cold start, inflating SSR bundle size and memory and corrupting byte-length metadata. // Serve binaries via SvelteKit static dir; only enumerate text assets if needed

  query: "?raw", import: "default", eager: true,
}) as Record<string, string>;

---
title: Getting started
description: Configure a TypeScript runtime and mount owned routes.
---

Install the runtime, provider package, and shared adapters:

```sh
npm install plugfn @plugfn/providers @plugfn/client @superfunctions/db @superfunctions/http
```

```ts
import { createPlugFnRouter, plugFn } from "plugfn";
import { githubProvider } from "@plugfn/providers";

const plug = plugFn({
  database: adapter,
  auth: authProvider,
  baseUrl: "https://app.example.com",
  encryptionKey: process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY!,
  integrations: { github: { clientId: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID!, clientSecret: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET! } },
});
plug.providers.register(githubProvider);
const router = createPlugFnRouter(plug);
```

Supply a durable database adapter, a real authentication provider, and secrets from the deployment environment. Mount the router through a `@superfunctions/http` framework adapter under an application path such as `/api/plugfn`. The [source setup guide](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/plugfn/docs/getting-started.md) has Express, Fastify, and Hono examples plus the full route list.

## Application-owned setup and mounting

Keep construction in a server-only module. The following factory accepts the host's durable database and verified session resolver explicitly:

```ts
import express from "express";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";
import { toExpress } from "@superfunctions/http-express";
import { plugFn, createPlugFnRouter, type PlugFnPrincipal } from "plugfn";
import { githubProvider } from "@plugfn/providers";

function required(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing ${name}`);
  return value;
}
export async function createIntegrationApp(
  database: Adapter,
  authenticate: (request: Request) => Promise<PlugFnPrincipal | null>,
) {
  const plug = plugFn({
    database,
    auth: { authenticate },
    baseUrl: required("APP_URL"),
    encryptionKey: required("PLUGFN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"),
    workflows: {
      runtime: { actions: { recordPush: async (context) => ({ event: context.trigger.event }) } },
    },
    integrations: {
      github: {
        clientId: required("GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"),
        clientSecret: required("GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
      },
    },
  });
  plug.providers.register(githubProvider);
  await plug.ready;
  const app = express();
  // Keep original bytes for webhook signature verification.
  app.use(express.raw({ type: "*/*", limit: "2mb" }));
  app.use("/api/plugfn", toExpress(createPlugFnRouter(plug)));
  return { app, plug };
}
```

Install `express @superfunctions/http-express` as well as the packages above. Call this factory from your host bootstrap, then `app.listen(...)` or mount the returned app in your existing Express server. Provision PlugFn's `getSchema()` tables with the host migration system first. `plug.ready` rejects if persisted workflow triggers cannot be restored; do not report the service ready before it resolves.

`PLUGFN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is a 32-byte key encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters. Generate and store it once in the deployment's secret manager; changing it without migrating encrypted connection state makes stored credentials unreadable. Set `APP_URL` to the application's public URL. Register the exact callback URI, such as `https://app.example.com/api/plugfn/callback/github`, with the provider and supply that URI when starting the connection.

The host resolver returns an authenticated `userId` and, where applicable, `tenantId`. Returning null denies protected routes. Browser-supplied owner fields do not replace that identity. Continue with [Connections and OAuth](/docs/connections-and-oauth) and [Actions, workflows, and sync](/docs/workflows-and-sync).
---
title: Provider readiness
description: Use per-provider status and the release gate together.
---

The [readiness matrix](/docs/reference/readiness) is the public source of truth. GitHub, Linear, ClickUp, and Gmail are the core cross-language set; Notion is beta overall because Python parity is unsupported. Adjacent providers can be experimental, and inbound mail connectors are vertical-only. Unlisted providers are unsupported by default.

A provider is production-ready only when the matrix marks it `production` **and** `npm run gate:plugfn-release` passes on the same commit. Presence in the source tree or a passing provider-specific test alone is insufficient. Check the exact TypeScript and Python columns before adoption.
---
title: Python runtime
description: Assess the experimental Python surface per provider.
---

The Python `plugfn` package is an experimental baseline. It exports the declared core provider set of GitHub, Linear, ClickUp, and Gmail, but does not match the full TypeScript provider surface.

```sh
pip install plugfn
```

The [Python source guide](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/plugfn/python/README.md) shows its setup shape. Check the matrix's Python column for each provider and avoid assuming parity with TypeScript.
---
title: Workflows and sync
description: Run provider actions and persisted integration jobs.
---

PlugFn coordinates provider actions, workflows, sync jobs, checkpoints, events, and metrics. The TypeScript router includes workflow discovery, sync-job create/list/get/cancel, checkpoint upsert, event list, and metrics routes. Keep workflow execution server-side and authorize it against the derived principal.

The release contract describes DB-backed idempotent workflow resume. Process-local delay timers are not considered production-safe; delay steps fail closed until a durable scheduler exists. Read the [release gates](/docs/reference/release-gates) and [provider throttle runbook](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/plugfn/docs/runbooks/provider-throttle-incident.md).

## Execute an action on the server

Use the `plug` instance from [setup](/docs/getting-started). Derive the actor from the host's verified session and select a connection owned by that actor:

```ts
import type { PlugFn, PlugFnActor } from "plugfn";

export async function listRepositories(plug: PlugFn, actor: PlugFnActor, connectionId: string) {
  return plug.action("github", "repos.list", {
    userId: actor.userId,
    actor,
    connectionId,
    params: { visibility: "all", startPage: 1, maxPages: 1 },
    cache: false,
  });
}
```

The result is the action's data (an array for `repos.list`), not an HTTP envelope. A missing provider/action, invalid parameters, unavailable connection, or provider failure rejects the promise. Use the provider's parameter schema and connection scopes; do not forward arbitrary browser action names or credentials into this helper. Retry only operations whose semantics are safe to repeat.

## Queue and inspect a sync job

Register `gmailProvider` from `@plugfn/providers` on the server, configure its OAuth application, and connect Gmail with the scopes required by `mail.sync`. The browser client can then request an authorized sync job; the server worker performs it:

```ts
import { createPlugFnClient } from "@plugfn/client";
const client = createPlugFnClient({ baseUrl: "/api/plugfn", credentials: "include" });
const connections = await client.listConnections({ provider: "gmail" });
const connection = connections.find((item) => item.status === "active");
if (!connection) throw new Error("Connect Gmail first");
const job = await client.createSyncJob({
  provider: "gmail", connectionId: connection.id, resource: "messages", mode: "full",
});
console.log(job.id, job.status);
const current = await client.getSyncJob(job.id);
console.log(current.fetchedCount, current.persistedCount, current.error);
// Optional user cancellation: await client.cancelSyncJob(job.id);
```

Resource identifiers are provider-defined; confirm them in that provider's sync definition. A queued job does not run itself. In an authorized server worker, call `await plug.sync.processQueued({ limit: 10 })` on the application's schedule. Register a persistence sink before expecting fetched records to reach your application's database, and inspect `persistedCount` separately from `fetchedCount`. The browser client manages jobs and checkpoints; it does not execute arbitrary provider actions.

## Persisted workflows

The high-level facade exposes listing, enable/disable/delete, statistics, and trigger rehydration for stored workflows. It does not expose a `plug.workflows.create()` or browser workflow execution method. Hosts can author stored definitions through `AdapterWorkflowStorage`, register serializable action names through `workflows.runtime`, and activate them with `plug.workflows.enable(id)`.

```ts
import { AdapterWorkflowStorage, WorkflowStatus, type PlugFn, type PlugFnActor } from "plugfn";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";

export async function createWorkflow(database: Adapter, plug: PlugFn, actor: PlugFnActor) {
  const storage = new AdapterWorkflowStorage(database);
  const workflow = await storage.create({
    userId: actor.userId, tenantId: actor.tenantId,
    name: "Handle a push",
    status: WorkflowStatus.Disabled,
    definition: {
      trigger: { provider: "github", event: "push" },
      steps: [{ type: "action", id: "record-push", action: "recordPush" }],
    },
  });
  await plug.workflows.enable(workflow.id);
  return workflow.id;
}
```

The setup factory registers `recordPush` to return the trigger event name; the workflow engine records that result. Replace it with your authorized application operation when needed. Keep implementations in trusted server code and references in the stored definition. The host must authorize workflow authoring; direct storage access is not an HTTP authorization boundary. Trigger activation also requires the provider's verified webhook setup. Test duplicate delivery and restart behavior before production adoption. Delay steps currently fail closed without durable scheduling.

---
title: Readiness source guide
description: Authoritative PlugFn source document.
---

This matrix is the public source of truth for provider readiness. A provider is not production-ready unless:

1. this matrix marks it `production`
2. the repo-root PlugFn release gate passes on the same commit

Unlisted providers are unsupported by default.

Important: a `production` row means the provider contract and parity scope are the intended release target. The provider is only production-ready on a given commit when the repo-root PlugFn release gate is also green on that same commit.

## Status vocabulary

- `production`: release-gated and approved for default adoption
- `beta`: useful and intentionally supported, but not yet release-gated
- `experimental`: present but still under hardening or incomplete
- `vertical-only`: useful for a specific product or mail workflow, not part of the default shared-runtime adoption story
- `unsupported`: not currently available for adoption

## Core provider set tracked by the release gate

The minimum provider set that the release gate tracks is:

- `github`
- `linear`
- `clickup`
- `gmail`
- `notion`

## Matrix

| Provider | Scope | Overall status | TypeScript readiness | Python readiness | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| github | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| linear | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| clickup | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| gmail | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| notion | core | beta | production | unsupported | TypeScript provider is release-gated for Nucleum adoption; overall status stays beta until Python parity exists. |
| slack | adjacent | experimental | experimental | experimental | Present in both trees, but not part of the declared core release set. |
| discord | adjacent | experimental | experimental | unsupported | TypeScript-only today. |
| stripe | adjacent | experimental | experimental | unsupported | TypeScript-only today. |
| outlook | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound Microsoft Graph mail connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| yahoo | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound OAuth IMAP connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| icloud | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound app-password IMAP connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| imap-smtp | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Compatibility provider ID for the generic inbound IMAP connector; SMTP delivery is SendFn scope. |

## Interpretation rules

- Do not convert `beta`, `experimental`, or `vertical-only` entries into blanket production claims.

Mount the router through a `@superfunctions/http` framework adapter under an application path such as `/api/plugfn`. ## Application-owned setup and mounting

Keep construction in a server-only module. The following factory accepts the host's durable database and verified session resolver explicitly:

```ts
import express from "express";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";
import { toExpress } from "@superfunctions/http-express";
import { plugFn, createPlugFnRouter, type PlugFnPrincipal } from "plugfn";
import { githubProvider } from "@plugfn/providers";

function required(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) throw new Error(`Missing ${name}`);
  return value;
}
export async function createIntegrationApp(
  database: Adapter,
  authenticate: (request: Request) => Promise<PlugFnPrincipal | null>,
) {
  const plug = plugFn({
    database,
    auth: { authenticate },
    baseUrl: required("APP_URL"),
    encryptionKey: required("PLUGFN_ENCRYPTION_KEY"),
    workflows: {
      runtime: { actions: { recordPush: async (context) => ({ event: context.trigger.event }) } },
    },
    integrations: {
      github: {
        clientId: required("GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"),
        clientSecret: required("GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
      },
    },
  });

  await plug.ready;

  app.use(express.raw({ type: "*/*", limit: "2mb" }));

  return { app, plug };
}
```

title: Workflows and sync
description: Run provider actions and persisted integration jobs.
---

PlugFn coordinates provider actions, workflows, sync jobs, checkpoints, events, and metrics. The TypeScript router includes workflow discovery, sync-job create/list/get/cancel, checkpoint upsert, event list, and metrics routes. Keep workflow execution server-side and authorize it against the derived principal.

The release contract describes DB-backed idempotent workflow resume. Process-local delay timers are not considered production-safe; delay steps fail closed until a durable scheduler exists. Read the [release gates](/docs/reference/release-gates) and [provider throttle runbook](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/plugfn/docs/runbooks/provider-throttle-incident.md).

## Execute an action on the server

Use the `plug` instance from [setup](/docs/getting-started). Derive the actor from the host's verified session and select a connection owned by that actor:

```ts
import type { PlugFn, PlugFnActor } from "plugfn";

export async function listRepositories(plug: PlugFn, actor: PlugFnActor, connectionId: string) {
  return plug.action("github", "repos.list", {
    userId: actor.userId,
    actor,
    connectionId,
    params: { visibility: "all", startPage: 1, maxPages: 1 },
    cache: false,
  });
}
```

The result is the action's data (an array for `repos.list`), not an HTTP envelope. A missing provider/action, invalid parameters, unavailable connection, or provider failure rejects the promise. Use the provider's parameter schema and connection scopes; do not forward arbitrary browser action names or credentials into this helper. Retry only operations whose semantics are safe to repeat.

## Queue and inspect a sync job

Register `gmailProvider` from `@plugfn/providers` on the server, configure its OAuth application, and connect Gmail with the scopes required by `mail.sync`. The browser client can then request an authorized sync job; the server worker performs it:

```ts
import { createPlugFnClient } from "@plugfn/client";
const client = createPlugFnClient({ baseUrl: "/api/plugfn", credentials: "include" });
const connections = await client.listConnections({ provider: "gmail" });
const connection = connections.find((item) => item.status === "active");
if (!connection) throw new Error("Connect Gmail first");
const job = await client.createSyncJob({
  provider: "gmail", connectionId: connection.id, resource: "messages", mode: "full",
});
console.log(job.id, job.status);
const current = await client.getSyncJob(job.id);
console.log(current.fetchedCount, current.persistedCount, current.error);
// Optional user cancellation: await client.cancelSyncJob(job.id);
```

Resource identifiers are provider-defined; confirm them in that provider's sync definition. A queued job does not run itself. In an authorized server worker, call `await plug.sync.processQueued({ limit: 10 })` on the application's schedule. Register a persistence sink before expecting fetched records to reach your application's database, and inspect `persistedCount` separately from `fetchedCount`. The browser client manages jobs and checkpoints; it does not execute arbitrary provider actions.

## Persisted workflows

The high-level facade exposes listing, enable/disable/delete, statistics, and trigger rehydration for stored workflows. It does not expose a `plug.workflows.create()` or browser workflow execution method. Hosts can author stored definitions through `AdapterWorkflowStorage`, register serializable action names through `workflows.runtime`, and activate them with `plug.workflows.enable(id)`.

```ts
import { AdapterWorkflowStorage, WorkflowStatus, type PlugFn, type PlugFnActor } from "plugfn";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";

export async function createWorkflow(database: Adapter, plug: PlugFn, actor: PlugFnActor) {
  const storage = new AdapterWorkflowStorage(database);
  const workflow = await storage.create({
    userId: actor.userId, tenantId: actor.tenantId,
    name: "Handle a push",
    status: WorkflowStatus.Disabled,
    definition: {
      trigger: { provider: "github", event: "push" },
      steps: [{ type: "action", id: "record-push", action: "recordPush" }],
    },
  });
  await plug.workflows.enable(workflow.id);
  return workflow.id;
}
```

The setup factory registers `recordPush` to return the trigger event name; the workflow engine records that result. Replace it with your authorized application operation when needed. Keep implementations in trusted server code and references in the stored definition. The host must authorize workflow authoring; direct storage access is not an HTTP authorization boundary. Trigger activation also requires the provider's verified webhook setup. Test duplicate delivery and restart behavior before production adoption. Delay steps currently fail closed without durable scheduling.

---
title: Readiness source guide
description: Authoritative PlugFn source document.
---

This matrix is the public source of truth for provider readiness. A provider is not production-ready unless:

1. this matrix marks it `production`
2. the repo-root PlugFn release gate passes on the same commit

Unlisted providers are unsupported by default.

Important: a `production` row means the provider contract and parity scope are the intended release target. The provider is only production-ready on a given commit when the repo-root PlugFn release gate is also green on that same commit.

## Status vocabulary

- `production`: release-gated and approved for default adoption
- `beta`: useful and intentionally supported, but not yet release-gated
- `experimental`: present but still under hardening or incomplete
- `vertical-only`: useful for a specific product or mail workflow, not part of the default shared-runtime adoption story
- `unsupported`: not currently available for adoption

## Core provider set tracked by the release gate

The minimum provider set that the release gate tracks is:

- `github`
- `linear`
- `clickup`
- `gmail`
- `notion`

## Matrix

| Provider | Scope | Overall status | TypeScript readiness | Python readiness | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| github | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| linear | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| clickup | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| gmail | core | production | production | production | Core provider contract exists in both languages; final production-ready claim still depends on the repo-root release gate. |
| notion | core | beta | production | unsupported | TypeScript provider is release-gated for Nucleum adoption; overall status stays beta until Python parity exists. |
| slack | adjacent | experimental | experimental | experimental | Present in both trees, but not part of the declared core release set. |
| discord | adjacent | experimental | experimental | unsupported | TypeScript-only today. |
| stripe | adjacent | experimental | experimental | unsupported | TypeScript-only today. |
| outlook | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound Microsoft Graph mail connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| yahoo | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound OAuth IMAP connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| icloud | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Inbound app-password IMAP connector; outbound delivery is SendFn scope. |
| imap-smtp | vertical | vertical-only | vertical-only | unsupported | Compatibility provider ID for the generic inbound IMAP connector; SMTP delivery is SendFn scope. |

## Interpretation rules

- Do not convert `beta`, `experimental`, or `vertical-only` entries into blanket production claims.
- Do not assume source-tree presence equals supported adoption.
- Python parity for the core set is now tracked provider-by-provider in this matrix rather than by blanket language claims.

---
title: Release Gates source guide
description: Authoritative PlugFn source document.
---

## Canonical command

The authoritative repo-root release proof is:

```bash
npm run gate:plugfn-release
```

This command is the only supported global readiness check for PlugFn. It emits a deterministic JSON result with step status, docs inventory status, and the final production-claim rule.

## Gate coverage

`npm run gate:plugfn-release` proves all of the following from the repository root:

1. `npm --prefix plugfn/core run build`
2. `npm --prefix plugfn/core run type-check`
3. `npm --prefix plugfn/core test -- --run`
4. `npm --prefix plugfn/core test -- --run tests/e2e/oauth-callback.test.ts tests/e2e/webhook-verification.test.ts`
5. `npm --prefix plugfn/client run build`
6. `npm --prefix plugfn/client run typecheck`
7. `npm --prefix plugfn/client test -- --run`
8. `npm --prefix plugfn/providers run build`
9. `npm --prefix plugfn/providers run typecheck`
10. `npm --prefix plugfn/providers test -- --run`
11. provider-specific gates:
   - `npm run gate:plugfn-provider-github`
   - `npm run gate:plugfn-provider-linear`
   - `npm run gate:plugfn-provider-clickup`
   - `npm run gate:plugfn-provider-gmail`
   - `npm run gate:plugfn-provider-notion`
12. `npm --prefix plugfn/cli run build`
13. `npm --prefix plugfn/cli run type-check`
14. `npm --prefix plugfn/cli test -- --run`
15. `python3 -m pytest -q plugfn/python/tests`
16. docs/status inventory checks for:
   - portable paths in public docs
   - package-name truth
   - current gate wording
   - readiness-matrix coverage for `github`, `linear`, `clickup`, `gmail`, and `notion`

## Production-ready claim rule

PlugFn still does not make blanket claims for every provider or vertical module.

A PlugFn provider or runtime surface may be described as production-ready only when both conditions are true on the same commit:

1. `npm run gate:plugfn-release` passes
2. the surface is marked `production` in [../provider-readiness-matrix.md](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/plugfn/docs/provider-readiness-matrix.md)

Anything outside that boundary remains `beta`, `experimental`, `vertical-only`, or `unsupported` according to the matrix.
